channel.description: Recent content in Customizable on Best of AI

item.title: ArborGold
item.description:
Arborists can build quotes from price lists, schedule crews, and send invoices from the field. Mobile apps let crews see jobs and update status. Customer history helps with repeat work and follow-ups.

It is aimed at small and mid-size companies. Features are practical rather than AI heavy.

Jobber and Housecall Pro are broader field service alternatives. ArborGold suits tree care businesses.

item.title: Shopmonkey
item.description:
Technicians and service advisors build estimates from labor guides and parts catalogs, send them to customers for approval, and track the job through completion. Digital vehicle inspections with photos help explain recommended work. Text messaging keeps customers informed.

Shops use it to replace paper tickets and spreadsheets. Parts ordering and accounting integrations vary by plan.

Tekmetric and Shop-Ware are close alternatives. Shopmonkey suits independent repair shops.

item.title: Tekmetric
item.description:
Service advisors write estimates, send digital inspections with photos, and collect approval and payment by text or email. Reports show car count, average repair order, and technician productivity. Integrations connect to parts suppliers and accounting software.

Shops use the data to see what is working and where jobs stall. It is a subscription product with per-shop pricing.

Shopmonkey and Shop-Ware are alternatives. Tekmetric suits independent shop owners and managers.

item.title: The Game Crafter
item.description:
Users upload artwork and choose components such as cards, boards, tokens, and boxes. Orders ship as single copies, so there is no minimum run. It also lets designers sell games through its shop.

Unit costs are higher than offset printing at volume, so it suits prototypes and small runs.

Print-on-demand services like Printerstudio are alternatives. The Game Crafter suits independent board game designers.

item.title: Zonos
item.description:
Merchants and brokers use it to classify products into tariff codes, estimate duties and taxes at checkout, and create paperwork. AI helps match product descriptions to HS codes. APIs plug into shops and carriers.

Classification still benefits from review for unusual goods.

Avalara and Flexport offer related services. Zonos suits customs brokers and cross-border sellers.

item.title: Azure AI Document Intelligence
item.description: Azure AI Document Intelligence reads documents so applications can use the data. Its layout model finds text, tables, headings, and selection marks, and prebuilt models recognize common document types such as invoices, receipts, business cards, identity documents, and many tax and mortgage forms, returning fields like totals, dates, and names with confidence scores. You can train custom models with a small number of examples to extract the fields in your own forms.

item.title: Azure AI Speech
item.description:
Azure AI Speech brings Microsoft’s speech technology into applications. Speech-to-text transcribes audio in real time or from recordings in many languages, with options for custom vocabulary and speaker separation. Text-to-speech offers a large library of neural voices in many languages and styles, with control over tone, speed, and emotion using SSML. Real-time speech translation converts spoken language into another language for captions or voice.

Additional features serve specialized needs. Custom Neural Voice lets approved customers build a branded voice from recorded samples, subject to a restricted-access process to prevent misuse. Voice live and conversational features support building voice agents, and avatar capabilities create talking presenters from text. Container deployments allow running models on premises or at the edge, and the service integrates with Azure OpenAI and other Azure AI tools.

item.title: Azure AI Vision
item.description:
Azure AI Vision gives developers pretrained image analysis. The Image Analysis service can describe an image in a sentence, tag objects and scenes, detect people and objects with locations, and extract printed and handwritten text through OCR. Additional capabilities include background removal, smart cropping, and searching images by meaning, using models that understand both text and images.

Video and spatial analysis features can analyze camera feeds to count people and measure how they move through physical spaces, useful in retail and building management. Face-related features exist but are limited by a responsible AI approval process, since facial recognition has privacy and fairness concerns. Customers can also train custom models for their own image categories, and containers allow running some features on the edge.

item.title: Google Document AI
item.description:
Document AI turns paper and PDF documents into structured data. Prebuilt processors read common document types: invoices with their line items, expense receipts, bank statements, government IDs, and forms. An OCR processor extracts text with layout information, and a layout parser prepares documents for use with language models by splitting them into meaningful chunks.

Customization is a strength. A custom extractor, based on Google’s Gemini models, can be set up with a few examples to pull specific fields from a company’s own documents, even if they vary in layout. A workbench lets teams train and evaluate processors, and a human-in-the-loop option sends uncertain results to reviewers. The output integrates with BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and workflow tools, which helps feed data to analytics and AI systems.

item.title: Justworks
item.description:
Justworks is aimed at small companies that don’t want to run HR in house. The platform handles payroll, tax filings, benefits enrollment, time off, onboarding, and compliance in a single system, with a mobile app for employees. Its HR support team helps with questions about employment rules.

The distinct feature is the co-employment model. Justworks operates as a professional employer organization, which means it becomes a co-employer for tax and insurance purposes, pooling its customers to buy group health insurance and workers compensation at rates a small firm could not get alone. The business keeps day-to-day control over its staff and hiring.

item.title: Kore.ai
item.description:
Kore.ai helps large organizations deploy virtual assistants. Companies design conversations and workflows in a low-code environment, connect them to back-end systems, and publish them on websites, mobile apps, messaging platforms, and voice lines. The assistants can answer questions and complete tasks such as resetting a password or checking a balance.

The platform has moved from rule-based dialogue to generative AI and agents. It supports large language models from several providers, retrieval over company content, and tools for building multi-agent systems, with governance features for testing and monitoring. Prebuilt solutions for banking, healthcare, retail, and HR speed up projects, and agent assist tools support human staff on live calls.

item.title: lemlist
item.description:
lemlist helps sales teams and agencies reach prospects at scale. Users build sequences that combine email, LinkedIn steps, and phone tasks, and personalize messages with variables such as name and company. The brand made its name with personalized images and videos that change for each recipient, a way to stand out in crowded inboxes.

Deliverability is a major part of the product. Inbox warm-up gradually builds sender reputation, and tools check domains and monitor placement so emails land in primary inboxes, not spam. A lead database lets users find contacts and verify emails, and AI helps write openers and suggest follow-ups.

item.title: LivePerson
item.description:
LivePerson began with live chat and developed into a conversational platform. Brands use it to let customers message them on the channels they already use, with a mix of human agents and automated assistants. The platform manages the conversations, routes them to the right team, and records the data.

AI is central. Bots handle common requests, such as order status or billing questions, and hand off to agents when needed, and agent assist tools suggest responses. The company offers tools for building and managing assistants powered by large language models, with guardrails and analytics to check quality and compliance. Customers include banks, telecoms, and retailers.

item.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365
item.description:
Dynamics 365 combines CRM and ERP in a modular set of cloud applications. The sales and customer service apps manage leads, opportunities, cases, and customer communications, while finance, supply chain, and Business Central handle accounting, inventory, purchasing, and operations. Because the modules share a data platform, a company can start with one and add others over time, and they connect closely with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Power BI.

Copilot is built throughout. In sales, it summarizes accounts and meetings, drafts emails, and suggests next steps. In service, it helps agents find answers and summarize cases, and in finance and supply chain, it supports tasks like reconciliations, collections, and spotting disruptions. AI agents take on routine tasks, such as qualifying leads or processing orders, and Copilot Studio lets companies build their own.

item.title: Optimizely
item.description:
Optimizely began as an A/B testing tool and grew into a suite for digital experiences. Teams use web experimentation to compare versions of pages, feature experimentation to test changes in apps behind feature flags, and personalization to show different content to different audiences. Statistical engines determine which variations win, and rollouts can be controlled to reduce risk.

The platform also includes content management and commerce. A CMS lets marketers create and manage web content, and commerce products support B2B and B2C stores, so a company can build, publish, test, and optimize in a single environment. AI features, under the Opal brand, help generate content, suggest experiment ideas, and run agents that automate steps in marketing workflows.

item.title: Planhat
item.description:
Planhat is a customer platform built for subscription businesses. It connects to a company’s tools and data, builds a profile for each account, and shows health, usage trends, revenue, and conversations in one place. Teams use it to prepare for renewals and spot upsell opportunities.

Automation and workflows trigger tasks and outreach when something changes, such as a drop in usage or an upcoming renewal. Dashboards and reports show retention and growth, and AI summarizes accounts and suggests actions.

item.title: Sierra
item.description:
Sierra focuses on replacing scripted chatbots with agents that can actually resolve customer issues. Companies such as consumer brands and subscription services deploy Sierra agents to answer questions, process returns, change plans, schedule appointments, and handle other tasks by connecting to back-end systems. The agent follows the company’s policies and tone, and hands off to a human when needed.

Several elements distinguish its approach. An Agent OS provides the tools for building, testing, and monitoring agents, with simulation and evaluation to catch problems before customers see them, and supports voice and messaging channels. The company often uses outcome-based pricing, where customers pay for resolved conversations instead of seats, which aligns cost with value. It combines multiple language models to improve reliability.

item.title: Storylane
item.description:
Storylane is an interactive demo platform. A user records their product with a browser extension that captures screenshots or the underlying page, then adds hotspots, tooltips, and callouts to guide viewers through a story. The result is a demo that prospects can click through on their own, without needing a sandbox or a live call.

Teams use it across the sales cycle. Marketing embeds demos on landing pages, sales sends personalized versions in outreach emails, and customer success uses them for onboarding. AI features add voiceovers, translations into other languages, and personalization of names and logos for each prospect. Analytics show who viewed a demo and where they dropped off.

item.title: Sumsub
item.description:
Sumsub provides identity verification for online services that must know who their customers are. A user photographs an ID document and takes a selfie, and Sumsub checks that the document is real, matches the person, and that a live person is present, which helps block stolen identities and deepfakes. Results come back in seconds or minutes.

Beyond onboarding, the platform covers compliance. It screens users against sanctions and politically exposed persons lists, monitors transactions for suspicious behavior, and supports business verification for companies. Fraud prevention features detect fake documents, duplicate accounts, and bots, and a case management dashboard lets compliance staff review flagged applicants.

item.title: Superwhisper
item.description:
Superwhisper is a dictation tool. You press a shortcut, speak, and the text appears wherever your cursor is, in an email, a document, or a code editor. Because it can run speech recognition models on your own machine, nothing has to be sent to the cloud, which matters for privacy and works without an internet connection.

Modes make it more than plain transcription. A mode can clean up filler words, format the text as an email or meeting notes, translate it, or follow a custom prompt that uses a language model to rewrite what you said. It also understands context from the app you are in, and supports many languages and voice models, including cloud options for higher accuracy.

item.title: Tavus
item.description:
Tavus builds AI humans. A person records a short sample, and the platform creates a digital replica that can speak a script, so one recording can become thousands of personalized videos with each viewer’s name and details. This suits sales outreach and customer communications.

The company also provides conversational video agents, which see and hear a user and respond in real time with a face and voice, through an API. Use cases include interviews, coaching, and customer service.

item.title: Vidyard
item.description:
Vidyard is a video platform for business teams. Salespeople record quick webcam or screen videos for prospects, send them by email or link, and see who watched and for how long. Marketers host videos on their websites with branded players and gated forms.

AI features speed up production. Script suggestions help with what to say, avatars let a rep send a personalized video without recording each one, and transcripts, summaries, and chapters make longer videos easier to use. Integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot put engagement data in the CRM.

item.title: Vimeo
item.description:
Vimeo started as a community for filmmakers and grew into a professional video platform. Businesses use it to host and share video without ads, embed customizable players on their websites, control who can watch, and see analytics on viewing. Features such as review tools, live streaming, and webinars support marketing, training, and internal communications.

AI features have been added to speed up work. Tools can generate scripts, create video from text or slides, produce captions and translations, and edit footage by removing filler words or creating highlights, and an AI assistant helps with chapters and summaries. Vimeo’s editing tools and recording app allow teams to produce video without separate software.

item.title: TattooJinn
item.description:
TattooJinn narrows image generation to tattoo art. A user types an idea and picks a style, such as traditional, fine line, or blackwork, and the tool creates design concepts. Variations help someone test placement and look before committing.

The designs work as inspiration for conversations with a tattoo artist, who adapts them to a body and a technique. AI images may include details that do not translate well to skin or may resemble existing artists’ work, so an artist should redraw or approve anything permanent.

item.title: ComplyAdvantage
item.description:
ComplyAdvantage provides financial crime tools for banks, fintechs, and other regulated firms. At onboarding, it checks whether a customer or company appears on sanctions lists, politically exposed person lists, or negative news, and continues to monitor them over time. Transaction monitoring flags unusual activity that may signal money laundering.

Its data comes from a large collection of sources that is structured and updated continuously, and machine learning ranks matches to cut down on false alarms that compliance staff would otherwise review by hand. Case management tools help analysts document decisions for regulators, and risk assessment features support a risk-based approach.

item.title: Duve
item.description:
Duve is a guest experience platform. Before arrival, guests receive a digital check-in flow, can upload documents, and see offers for upgrades and extras. During the stay, a messaging assistant answers questions about the property and the area, and requests are routed to staff when a person is needed.

The platform includes a digital guidebook, upsell tools that present add-ons at the right moment, and integration with property management systems. For hoteliers and vacation rental managers, this reduces repetitive messages and brings extra revenue per booking.

item.title: Keela
item.description:
Keela helps small and mid-sized nonprofits manage supporters. It keeps donor records, gifts, and communication history, processes online donations, runs email campaigns, and supports events and volunteer tracking. The platform aims to be affordable and approachable for teams without a dedicated data staff.

AI features guide outreach. Engagement scoring highlights supporters likely to give again or increase gifts, timing suggestions prompt contact when it is most effective, and a writing assistant drafts appeals and thank-you notes. Reports show campaign results and giving trends.

item.title: Productboard
item.description:
Productboard is a product management platform. Feedback from many sources flows into a central place, where it is linked to features and customers. Product managers see which problems come up most and who is asking, which grounds roadmap decisions in evidence.

AI helps process the volume of input. It groups similar requests, summarizes calls and tickets, and drafts specs and release notes. Prioritization frameworks score ideas against objectives, and roadmaps can be shared with stakeholders at different levels of detail.

item.title: Momentic Mo
item.description:
Mo takes an exploratory approach to testing. Instead of writing scripts for each test, a team points Mo at an app and supplies login credentials, and AI agents navigate the interface, trying flows, entering unusual inputs, and checking for errors or broken behavior. The agents report what they find.

Momentic’s wider platform helps teams write and maintain end-to-end tests in natural language, which reduces upkeep when interfaces change. Mo complements that by finding issues no one thought to test, like a human tester poking around.

item.title: Ando
item.description:
Ando rethinks team chat for a workplace where software agents work next to people. In most chat tools, AI is an add-on bot. In Ando, agents have identities, inboxes, and permissions, and they can join channels, read ongoing conversations, and message teammates, just like human members.

The product has the familiar parts of a messaging platform, including channels, direct messages, group conversations, and calls. The difference is how agents are treated: a person can assign work to an agent in a thread, and the agent can respond, ask questions, and report back. Teams can bring agents built on different models.

item.title: Scholé
item.description:
Scholé rethinks workplace learning. Instead of asking employees to finish courses on the side, it delivers short, relevant learning moments tied to real tasks, adapting to what a person already knows and needs to do. Principles from learning science, such as practice and spaced repetition, shape the design.

Teams can use it to build skills in areas like communication, sales, or technical topics, with AI creating content and feedback. The idea is learning that fits into work and sticks.

item.title: Enlive
item.description:
Enlive is a prompt layer. Instead of writing a long, careful prompt, a user types a brief request, and Enlive expands it with relevant context, structure, and instructions before sending it to a model. The idea is to get better answers from people who are not prompt engineers.

It works across multiple models and tracks preferences, such as tone and format, so later requests fit the user’s habits. This addresses the common experience that vague prompts return vague answers. For power users it can save the time spent rewriting prompts.

item.title: QueryStory
item.description:
QueryStory approaches analytics with agents. A team connects its data sources and describes the business, such as its metrics and definitions, and then asks questions in natural language. The agents write queries, analyze results, and respond with explanations and visuals.

The point is to go beyond a static chart. When a number moves, a user can ask why, and the agent investigates by looking at breakdowns and related data. Business context helps the agent interpret questions the way an analyst on the team would.

item.title: Encore AI
item.description:
Encore AI builds on conversation data. It analyzes recordings of calls and chats to learn which behaviors lead to good outcomes, such as how top reps handle objections or open a conversation. Those patterns become the basis for AI agents that talk with customers.

The agents can take calls or messages themselves or support human reps with live guidance. The idea is to scale the best performers’ approach across a team instead of relying on training alone. Companies with large volumes of calls and recorded history are the target.

item.title: OpenAI Presence
item.description:
Presence aims to let companies put OpenAI-powered agents on the front line of conversations. Businesses configure agents that talk with customers by phone or chat and handle employee requests, connecting them to company systems so they can look up information and take actions.

The platform combines the models with enterprise features: tools for building and testing agents, integrations, monitoring, and controls to keep agents within policy. It competes with specialized customer service AI vendors and with platforms from other model providers.

item.title: Algolia AI Search
item.description:
Algolia is a hosted search service known for speed. Developers send it their data, such as products, articles, or help center pages, and use its APIs and UI libraries to add search that responds as the user types, with typo tolerance, filters, and facets. Many e-commerce and media sites use it.

Its AI search layer extends that with newer methods. Hybrid search blends keyword matching with vector similarity so queries find results by meaning, and tools can personalize ranking from user behavior. Merchandisers can adjust relevance with business rules without code, and the platform supports retrieval for conversational and agent experiences, where an AI model answers using the retrieved content.

item.title: FLUX
item.description: FLUX comes from Black Forest Labs, a company founded by researchers who previously worked on Stable Diffusion. Its models became popular because they produce sharp, detailed images that follow prompts closely, including difficult cases like readable text in a picture and complex scenes with several subjects. For many people, FLUX became the best open alternative to closed services such as Midjourney, because the weights for several versions can be downloaded and used locally.

item.title: Tencent Cloud ADP
item.description:
Tencent Cloud ADP gives companies tools to create agents. Users connect knowledge bases for retrieval, design workflows with a visual editor, and combine agents that work together. Models include Tencent’s Hunyuan family and others.

Typical applications are customer service, internal assistants, and process automation. The platform includes tools for testing and monitoring and integrates with Tencent’s ecosystem, including WeChat and enterprise messaging.

It is sold on usage-based pricing within Tencent Cloud. Outside China, availability and support are more limited, and organizations must consider data residency. Alternatives include Alibaba Cloud’s Bailian, Baidu Qianfan, ByteDance’s Volcano Engine, Dify, and AWS Bedrock Agents. Tencent Cloud ADP suits companies building agents on Tencent Cloud.

item.title: Amplemarket
item.description:
Amplemarket helps sales teams find and contact potential customers. It combines a database of B2B contacts and companies with search filters and intent signals, so reps can build lists of people who match their ideal customer and show signs of interest, such as hiring, funding, or website activity. Contact data is verified and enriched to reduce bounced emails and wrong numbers.

Outreach happens through multichannel sequences that mix email, phone calls, and social steps such as LinkedIn messages. A parallel dialer lets reps call through lists quickly. The AI layer researches each account and prospect, drafts personalized emails and call notes, and surfaces the best people to contact first. Duo Intelligence is Amplemarket’s approach of AI preparing the work while the rep reviews and sends, instead of fully automatic sending.

item.title: Bloomfire
item.description:
Bloomfire is a knowledge management platform. Employees add articles, files, videos, and Q&A to a central library, tag them, and find them later with search. The platform is meant to hold what a company knows so that people do not keep asking colleagues the same questions.

AI features make retrieval easier. Users ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn from the company’s own content with links to sources, and the system can suggest related material and flag content that needs updating. Analytics show what people search for and where gaps exist.

item.title: C3.ai
item.description:
C3.ai builds packaged AI applications and a platform for developing them. Instead of starting from scratch, a company can adopt an application for a defined problem, such as predicting when equipment will fail, detecting fraud, or optimizing inventory, and connect it to their data. The platform provides tools for data integration, modeling, and deployment.

The company has moved to add generative AI. Its offerings include tools that let users ask questions about enterprise data in natural language and agent features for business workflows. Customers include utilities, manufacturers, banks, and defense and government agencies, where large-scale deployments are common.

item.title: ChurnZero
item.description:
ChurnZero is built for customer success teams at software-as-a-service companies. It pulls in product usage data, support tickets, and CRM information to give each account a health score, so a team can see which customers are thriving and which are at risk of leaving before a renewal conversation turns bad.

Automation handles routine outreach. Playbooks trigger tasks and emails when a customer hits a milestone or goes quiet, in-app messages guide users inside the product, and dashboards track renewals, adoption, and revenue. AI features summarize accounts, draft messages, and suggest next actions, and a customer-facing portal can share progress with clients.

item.title: Gainsight
item.description:
Gainsight was one of the first platforms for the customer success discipline. It pulls usage, support, survey, and billing data to produce a health score for every customer, so teams can see who needs attention before a renewal is at risk. Playbooks guide the steps a manager should take for each situation.

AI features predict churn, suggest next actions, summarize account history, and draft communications. Surveys, in-app engagement, and a community product complete the suite, and the company has expanded into customer education. Reports help leaders show the effect of customer success on retention.

item.title: Glassbox
item.description:
Glassbox captures user sessions on digital properties. Teams can replay a visit to see what a customer clicked, where they hesitated, and what errors they hit. Heatmaps summarize click and scroll behavior across many sessions, pointing to confusing pages or broken flows.

The platform adds analytics and detection. Journey analysis shows where users leave a funnel, and automatic detection flags frustration signals such as repeated clicks. It has features for regulated industries like banking, including data masking so that sensitive information is not stored. The company has expanded through acquisitions into areas like anomaly detection.

item.title: Instapage
item.description:
Instapage focuses on the page that visitors reach after clicking an ad. Marketers build pages in a drag-and-drop editor with templates, connect them to ad campaigns, and track conversion rates. Collaboration features let teams and clients comment directly on designs.

Optimization tools set it apart. A/B testing compares versions, heatmaps show where visitors engage, and personalization changes page content depending on the ad or audience that sent the visitor. AI helps write copy and suggests improvements.

item.title: Kommunicate
item.description:
Kommunicate combines a chatbot builder with a shared inbox for agents. Businesses add a chat widget to their site or app, train a bot on help articles and FAQs, and let it answer routine questions, handing the conversation to a person when the bot cannot help or the customer asks.

The platform supports generative AI models and connects to knowledge bases, so answers draw on company content. Multi-channel support extends to messaging apps, and analytics show deflection rates and satisfaction. Integrations with CRMs and helpdesks keep data in sync.

item.title: Landbot
item.description:
Landbot lets non-developers design conversations visually. A user drags blocks onto a canvas to ask questions, branch based on answers, and connect to other tools, then publishes the flow on a website, a landing page, or WhatsApp. The conversational format often gets more responses than a plain form.

AI features add the ability to answer free-text questions from a knowledge base and to build flows from a description. Integrations send leads to CRMs and spreadsheets, and handoff routes complex chats to human agents. Templates cover lead generation, support, and onboarding.

item.title: Lifesum
item.description:
Lifesum helps people understand what they eat. Users set a goal such as weight loss, maintenance, or muscle gain, then log food and drink by searching, scanning barcodes, or snapping photos. The app shows calories, macros, and nutrient balance, and gives feedback through scores and summaries.

Meal plans and recipes support particular diets, such as low carb, Mediterranean, or intermittent fasting. Integrations with fitness trackers and health apps bring in activity data. AI features help with logging foods from photos and offer personalized suggestions.

item.title: ManyChat
item.description: ManyChat lets businesses and creators respond to people in direct messages at scale. A visual flow builder defines how a conversation proceeds: someone comments a keyword on an Instagram post, ManyChat sends a DM with a link or a guide, asks questions, collects an email address, and tags the contact. It is widely used by influencers and online businesses to deliver lead magnets, run giveaways, and sell products through chat.

item.title: Promptfoo
item.description:
Promptfoo helps developers test AI systems systematically. A user defines test cases and criteria in a configuration file, runs prompts across models, and compares outputs side by side, with assertions that check for expected content, format, or safety. It runs from the command line and in CI pipelines.

Red-teaming features generate adversarial inputs to probe for jailbreaks, prompt injection, data leaks, and other vulnerabilities, and report where an application fails. It supports many providers and local models and has been widely adopted.

item.title: ScrapeGraph AI
item.description:
ScrapeGraph AI lets developers describe what they want from a page. A user supplies a URL and a prompt such as list every product name and price, and the library fetches the page, passes it to a language model, and returns structured data. It also builds graph pipelines for multi-page scraping.

The approach reduces the brittleness of selector-based scrapers, which break when layouts change. It supports local and cloud models, and a hosted API and no-code options exist.

item.title: Sprinklr
item.description:
Sprinklr serves very large organizations. It manages publishing across social channels, listens for brand mentions, handles customer care across messaging and voice, and analyzes market trends, using a shared data layer so teams see the whole customer picture.

AI runs through the platform: models classify conversations, detect sentiment, route cases, suggest replies, and generate content, and agents handle some customer interactions. Governance tools suit regulated industries and large teams.

Sprinklr is sold on enterprise subscriptions, with high cost and complexity. Alternatives include Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Khoros, Emplifi, and Salesforce. Sprinklr suits large brands managing many channels.

item.title: Stack AI
item.description:
Stack AI offers a visual builder for AI workflows. Users drag together components such as inputs, language models, document search, and outputs, then connect them to enterprise tools. The result can be deployed as a chatbot, form, or API.

Common cases include document processing, internal knowledge assistants, and support triage. The platform emphasizes security and governance, with options for private deployment. Templates give a starting point.

Stack AI has a free tier and paid plans. Workflows need testing and monitoring. Alternatives include Relevance AI, Dify, Flowise, n8n, and Microsoft Copilot Studio. Stack AI suits business teams building AI workflows without code.

item.title: SYSTRAN
item.description:
SYSTRAN is among the oldest names in machine translation. Its modern products use neural models, offered as an API, a desktop app, and server software that can run inside an organization’s own network. This matters for sensitive documents.

Customization lets organizations tune translation to their terminology, and the platform handles many file formats and language pairs. Government and corporate customers use it for large volumes of content.

SYSTRAN is sold by subscription and license. General-purpose language models now compete in translation quality. Alternatives include DeepL, Google Cloud Translation, Microsoft Translator, Amazon Translate, and Lilt. SYSTRAN suits organizations needing private, deployable translation.

item.title: Totango
item.description:
Totango helps subscription companies keep customers. It gathers usage and account data, scores health, and triggers playbooks when customers need attention. Modules called SuccessBLOCs package best-practice workflows that teams can adopt and adjust.

The company merged with Catalyst, another customer success platform, and the combined product serves teams from startups to enterprises. AI features summarize accounts and draft communications, and analytics show retention and expansion.

Totango has had a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Gainsight, ChurnZero, Planhat, Vitally, and HubSpot. Totango suits customer success teams at software companies.

item.title: Typeform
item.description:
Typeform changed the feel of online forms. Instead of showing a long page of fields, it presents one question at a time with large type and smooth transitions, which tends to make forms feel friendlier and often improves completion rates. People use it for surveys, quizzes, lead capture, registrations, feedback, and onboarding. Design options and templates make it easy to match a brand.

Behind the interface are capable features. Logic jumps change the next question based on earlier answers, calculators and scoring support quizzes, payments can be collected, and files can be uploaded. Integrations send responses to tools like Google Sheets, HubSpot, Slack, and Zapier. AI features help generate a form from a short prompt, suggest questions, and summarize responses so teams can understand results faster.

item.title: Writecream
item.description:
Writecream offers many small tools in one place. Users generate cold emails with personalized openers based on a prospect’s profile, write blog posts and ad copy, create images, and clone voices or make avatar videos.

Its outreach features appeal to sales teams that want personalization at scale, such as icebreakers for LinkedIn or email. Other tools cover general content needs.

Writecream has a free tier and paid plans. Generic AI personalization can feel obvious to recipients, and outreach must follow spam and privacy law. Alternatives include Lemlist, Copy.ai, Jasper, Instantly, and Clay. Writecream suits small teams wanting varied content tools.

item.title: Yellow.ai
item.description:
Yellow.ai builds AI agents for customer and employee service. A company connects it to systems such as CRMs and ticketing, trains it on content, and deploys across websites, messaging apps, and phone lines. The agents answer questions and complete tasks in many languages.

The platform emphasizes multilingual support, strong in markets such as India, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia. Tools for building, testing, and monitoring agents, along with analytics, support operations teams. Handoff to human agents is built in.

item.title: Qualtrics
item.description:
Qualtrics is an experience management platform. Organizations use it to run customer satisfaction surveys, product research, brand studies, and employee engagement programs. A powerful survey builder handles complex logic, and results flow into dashboards segmented by customer, team, or time.

AI features turn feedback into action. They analyze comments for sentiment and themes, spot issues as they emerge, predict which customers may leave, and suggest next steps. The platform also pulls in data from support calls, reviews, and social media.

item.title: Agiloft
item.description:
Agiloft is a configurable system for managing contracts from request to renewal. Teams create agreements from templates and clause libraries, route them through approvals, negotiate with redlining, collect signatures, and store them in a searchable repository. Alerts remind owners of renewals and obligations, and reports show how contracts are performing, so legal, procurement, and sales teams share a single source of truth.

Its design emphasizes flexibility without custom coding. Organizations can adjust fields, workflows, and rules through no-code tools, which suits companies with unusual processes, and it connects with systems such as Salesforce, SAP, and DocuSign. AI features extract data from existing contracts, identify risky or missing clauses, summarize agreements, and let users ask questions in plain language, which speeds up migration from messy archives.

item.title: Arcadia
item.description:
Arcadia has two sides. For consumers, it helps people use renewable energy even if they cannot install solar panels. Customers subscribe to a share of a local community solar project and receive credits on their utility bill, or choose plans that match their usage with renewable generation. The platform tracks bills and savings in one account.

For businesses, Arcadia offers access to utility data. It connects to thousands of utilities to pull bill and usage information through APIs, which energy software companies, solar developers, and sustainability teams use to analyze consumption. This data layer is a major part of its business and helps other companies build energy products.

item.title: Avalara
item.description: Avalara helps businesses get indirect taxes right. Sales tax rules vary by state, city, product type, and customer, and rates change often, which makes manual calculation risky. Avalara integrates with online stores, accounting software, and ERP systems to calculate the correct tax at checkout or invoicing based on the transaction’s location and product, then helps file returns and remit payments in many jurisdictions. It covers sales and use tax, VAT, and other transaction taxes around the world.

item.title: Character Creator
item.description: Character Creator lets artists build 3D characters without modeling every detail. You start with a base body, adjust shape sliders for face and body, and apply skin, hair, clothing, and accessories from a library. A rigged skeleton and facial controls come ready to animate, so a character can be used right away in games, films, and animations. Pipelines to Unreal Engine, Unity, Blender, Maya, and other tools make it practical in production.

item.title: Clarifai
item.description: Clarifai started as an image recognition API and has grown into a broader AI platform. Teams use it to find and call models for vision, language, and audio tasks, to train their own models on labeled data, and to run them in production. It includes tools for organizing and labeling data, searching images and video, and building workflows that chain several models together. Industries such as retail, media, and public sector have used it to classify content and find objects in large collections.

item.title: Datadog
item.description: Datadog is software-as-a-service for watching what your systems are doing. You install an agent on servers, containers, or cloud accounts, or connect it through one of hundreds of integrations, and it begins collecting metrics, logs, and traces. Dashboards and alerts then show how hosts, databases, queues, and services are behaving. The value for most teams is having infrastructure monitoring, application performance monitoring, log management, and real user monitoring in one place instead of stitching together separate tools.

item.title: Doxy.me
item.description:
Doxy.me gives clinicians a simple way to see patients by video. A provider gets a personal link; patients click it, enter a virtual waiting room, and join the visit in their browser with no account or app installation. That simplicity matters for patients who are not comfortable with technology, and it suits therapists, physicians, dietitians, speech and physical therapists, and other practitioners.

Beyond video, the paid tiers add features that clinics need. These include a customizable waiting room, patient check-in, screen sharing, group sessions, text message reminders, payments, and integrations with electronic health record systems. Administrators can manage a team of providers under one account, and the platform includes business associate agreements that healthcare organizations need under HIPAA. Newer AI tools offer note-taking from visits.

item.title: Fitbod
item.description: Fitbod creates workout plans without a human coach. At setup, you give your fitness level, goals, available equipment, and schedule, and it generates a session for each day. The routine adapts as you log sets, reps, and weights: it suggests weights and volume based on past performance, and it tracks which muscle groups have recovered, so you do not train the same area too hard on consecutive days. Videos demonstrate each exercise.

item.title: Flexport
item.description:
Flexport is a freight forwarder with a software platform. Companies that import and export goods book shipments, track containers, manage documents, and handle customs through a single interface, instead of coordinating by email with many parties. It also offers financing, warehousing, and trade services.

Technology handles repetitive work. AI reads shipping documents, checks customs data for errors, and predicts delays based on port, carrier, and weather information. An assistant answers questions about shipment status and helps with classification of goods. Data from many shipments feeds analytics on cost and performance.

item.title: Freeletics
item.description:
Freeletics grew out of bodyweight training. The app creates workout plans based on your goals, fitness level, available time, and equipment, with programs that range from short high-intensity sessions to longer strength and running plans. Videos demonstrate exercises, and you log workouts, so the plan can adjust to how you perform and how you feel.

An AI coach is at the center of the experience. It tailors weekly schedules, changes difficulty, and gives feedback, aiming to feel like a personal trainer at a fraction of the cost. The app also provides nutrition recommendations and recipes, mindfulness sessions, and community features. It works with smartwatches and other health apps.

item.title: Headspace
item.description:
Headspace is one of the best-known meditation apps, with a friendly style and a structured approach for beginners. It offers guided meditations of different lengths, sleep content, movement and breathing exercises, focus music, and courses on topics such as stress, anxiety, and relationships. Short daily sessions are designed to build a habit, and progress features encourage consistency.

The company has expanded beyond meditation into broader mental healthcare. Depending on the market and plan, users can access coaching and therapy services, and employers offer Headspace as a benefit. An AI companion, Ebb, provides conversational support for reflecting on feelings and finding relevant exercises. It is meant to support wellbeing, not to diagnose or treat conditions, and Headspace points users in crisis toward professional help.

item.title: Hive Moderation
item.description:
Hive offers content moderation as an API. A platform sends user uploads, such as photos, videos, livestreams, comments, or audio, and Hive returns classifications with confidence scores across categories like nudity, violence, hate symbols, drugs, and self-harm. Companies use these results to automatically remove content, send borderline cases to human reviewers, or restrict access, which would be impossible to do manually at scale.

The company’s models have broadened beyond traditional moderation. Hive offers AI-generated content detection to identify synthetic images, video, and audio, deepfake detection used by government and media customers, and tools for brand safety and contextual advertising. It trains on large human-labeled datasets, and customers can customize settings for their own policies.

item.title: Homer
item.description:
Homer is built for young children learning to read and explore. After parents enter a child’s age and interests, the app builds a learning path with activities that include phonics, letter sounds, sight words, stories, math, and creative play, and features content from well-known children’s brands. Lessons are short and playful, with characters and rewards that keep young learners engaged.

Personalization is a selling point: the program adapts to the child’s progress and interests, so a child who loves trains or animals gets content around those themes. Parents get progress reports and ideas for offline activities, and the app is designed to be used with limited screen time. Its approach follows early literacy research, and it has been used in homes and in some schools.

item.title: Kinedu
item.description:
Kinedu helps parents support their child’s early development. After entering a baby’s age, the app creates a plan with short, playful activities for each day, such as tummy time ideas, sensory games, and language exercises, with videos that show how to do them. Activities are grouped by areas like physical, cognitive, social-emotional, and language development.

The app tracks milestones and shows a baby’s progress against typical ranges, explaining what is normal and when to speak to a pediatrician. Articles and guidance from experts cover sleep, feeding, and parenting questions, and parents can keep a journal of moments. Some features use personalization to adjust suggestions to a child’s progress.

item.title: Lemonade
item.description:
Lemonade is an insurance company built around software. Customers get a quote and buy a policy in minutes through an app, chatting with an AI assistant called Maya instead of filling out long forms. The company covers renters, homeowners, car, pet, and term life insurance in various markets. Its pitch to younger customers has been a modern experience, low entry prices, and transparent terms.

AI shows up in operations. A claims bot named Jim can approve and pay simple claims quickly, sometimes within seconds, while complex cases go to human adjusters. Machine learning helps assess risk, detect fraud, and personalize pricing. The company is structured so that it takes a flat fee and uses the rest to pay claims, with unused money going to charities chosen by customers under its Giveback program.

item.title: Lexalytics
item.description: Lexalytics builds natural language processing for businesses that need to make sense of large amounts of text. Its Salience engine reads reviews, survey comments, support tickets, social posts, and call transcripts and returns structured information: whether the sentiment is positive or negative, which products or people are mentioned, what themes recur, and what the author intends. Analysts can then count, trend, and compare these signals instead of reading comments one by one.

item.title: Mapbox
item.description:
Mapbox is the mapping toolkit behind many apps. Developers use its SDKs to embed interactive maps in websites and in iOS and Android apps, with control over styles, layers, and data. Mapbox Studio lets designers customize map appearance, while vector tiles keep maps fast and sharp. Companies in logistics, travel, real estate, and mobility use it to show routes, locations, and live data.

The platform goes beyond display. APIs handle geocoding and search, turn-by-turn navigation, route optimization, isochrones that show how far you can get in a given time, and traffic-aware directions. A navigation SDK supports in-app guidance, and tools for working with large geospatial datasets allow analysis and visualization. Machine learning is used for features such as map matching and road data updates, and recent products add AI assistants for developers.

item.title: Mobalytics
item.description:
Mobalytics is a gaming analytics and coaching site. Players link their accounts, and the tool analyzes their games, scoring performance across areas like farming, vision, and teamfights. A profile shows trends over time and compares the player with others at their rank.

Coaching features set it apart. The platform highlights patterns in mistakes and suggests focus areas, offers guides for champions and builds, and provides an overlay with in-game tips. Premium plans add deeper analysis and AI-generated feedback.

item.title: MonkeyLearn
item.description:
MonkeyLearn let people analyze text without machine learning expertise. Teams could connect support tickets, survey responses, reviews, and social posts, pick a ready-made model for sentiment or topics, or train a custom classifier by tagging examples. Results appeared in dashboards and could be sent to spreadsheets, helpdesks, and BI tools, which made it popular with customer experience, product, and marketing teams.

Its approach was to make natural language processing approachable. A visual interface handled model creation and testing, and the API let developers add analysis to their own apps. Typical uses included tagging support requests by issue, tracking sentiment in reviews, and pulling themes from open-ended survey answers.

item.title: Nearmap
item.description:
Nearmap captures aerial photos from aircraft, covering large areas in populated regions, and refreshes them regularly. Users view and measure current imagery on a map, compare dates to see change over time, and download data for analysis.

AI turns pictures into data. Models detect features such as roof condition, solar panels, pools, vegetation, and building footprints, giving insurers, councils, and contractors information without visiting sites. The data is available through a web app, APIs, and integrations with GIS and other tools.

item.title: Okta
item.description:
Okta is one of the best-known providers of cloud identity. Companies use it as the central place where employees sign in to their applications: one login gives access to hundreds of apps through single sign-on, and multi-factor authentication adds protection against stolen passwords. The Universal Directory stores identities and groups, and lifecycle management automates giving people the right access when they join, change roles, or leave.

The platform covers more of the identity problem over time. Adaptive policies check device and context before allowing access, governance tools handle access reviews and requests, and privileged access tools protect administrator accounts. Okta also owns Auth0 for customer-facing apps. As companies deploy AI agents that act on behalf of users, Okta has added features for giving these agents their own identities and managing what they may do.

item.title: Persona
item.description:
Persona lets companies verify who their customers and business partners are. A business builds a flow, choosing which checks to run: collecting and verifying a government ID, matching a selfie to the photo with liveness detection, checking databases and watchlists, verifying a business and its owners, or confirming an address. The flow can adapt based on risk, asking for more evidence only when something looks suspicious.

Configurability sets it apart. Companies can design the user experience, set rules for approvals, and route uncertain cases to human reviewers in a case management tool. Additional products detect fraud patterns across accounts, run ongoing monitoring, and verify employees and workforce identities. APIs and no-code builders connect the flows to existing systems, and the platform covers documents from many countries.

item.title: Readwise
item.description:
Readwise addresses a common frustration: highlighting passages and never seeing them again. It imports highlights from Kindle, Apple Books, Instapaper, Pocket-style services, podcasts, and PDFs into one library, and sends a daily review of a few of them by email or in the app, using spaced repetition so important ideas return at intervals.

The service integrates with the note-taking ecosystem, exporting highlights to Notion, Obsidian, Roam, Logseq, and others, so notes stay linked to sources. Search lets you find a highlight across everything you have read, and a mobile and browser extension make capture easy. Readwise also makes Reader, a read-it-later app, and AI features can summarize and let you chat with your highlights.

item.title: Ready Player Me
item.description: Ready Player Me offered a way to carry one avatar across many apps. A user took a selfie or built a character in the creator, customized clothing and hair, and received a 3D avatar that worked in a growing network of games, social platforms, and VR worlds. For developers, an SDK and web tools made it easy to add avatars without building a character creator from scratch, and it supported engines such as Unity and Unreal.

item.title: Repustate
item.description: Repustate focuses on understanding opinions in many languages. Its API reads text, such as tweets, reviews, news, or survey responses, and returns the sentiment, the topics and entities discussed, and the themes that recur, with attention to context so that sentiment about one aspect of a product can be separated from another. Language coverage is a selling point, including Arabic, Chinese, and many other languages that are less well served by some competitors.

item.title: Satellogic
item.description:
Satellogic builds and operates its own satellites with the goal of making high-resolution imagery affordable and frequent. Its NewSat satellites capture sharp images and multispectral and hyperspectral data, and the company has emphasized low production costs, which allows it to launch many satellites and offer tasking and archive imagery. Customers use the data for mapping, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, defense, and environmental analysis.

The company layers analytics on top of imagery. Machine learning detects objects and changes, such as new construction or vehicle movement, and produces insights at scale, and cloud tools and APIs let customers search the archive and request new captures. It also provides satellites and data to government customers for sovereign needs.

item.title: Spire Global
item.description:
Spire builds and operates a large fleet of small satellites known as nanosatellites. Instead of taking photographs, they listen: they pick up radio signals from ships, aircraft, and GPS signals bouncing off the Earth, and measure atmospheric conditions. The resulting data feeds products that track vessels around the world, monitor air traffic, and improve weather forecasts.

The business sells data and analytics as a service. Maritime customers use it to follow ships, estimate arrival times, and detect suspicious behavior, aviation customers use it for flight tracking, and meteorological agencies use radio occultation data to enhance forecasts. Spire also provides space services, building and operating satellites for customers. Machine learning supports forecasting and anomaly detection in the data, and APIs deliver it to customers’ systems.

item.title: Stem AI
item.description:
Stem began by installing battery storage systems for businesses, and its software, Athena, became the heart of the company. Athena uses forecasts of energy prices, demand, and generation to decide when a battery should charge or discharge, balancing cost savings for the owner with revenue from grid services. This kind of optimization can make storage economically viable.

The business has shifted from selling hardware toward software and services. Athena manages solar plus storage, standalone batteries, and other distributed assets for developers and owners, and also offers analytics and asset performance tools. Machine learning helps predict conditions and handle the complexity of electricity markets, which differ by region.

item.title: Stripe
item.description: Stripe began as a way for developers to accept card payments with a few lines of code and has become the payment layer for much of the internet. Businesses use it to take cards and local payment methods online and in person, bill customers on subscription plans, send invoices, and pay out sellers on marketplaces. Its documentation and libraries are widely admired, which is why startups tend to adopt it first. It operates in many countries and currencies.

item.title: Tonic AI
item.description:
Tonic.ai solves a common development problem: engineers need realistic data to test software, but production data contains sensitive information. Tonic Structural connects to a database, identifies sensitive fields, and replaces them with fake but realistic values, preserving relationships and formats so applications behave as they would with real data. This allows teams to build and test with representative data without exposing customers’ details.

Other products broaden the range. Tonic Fabricate generates synthetic data from scratch for new applications or demos, and Tonic Textual finds and redacts sensitive information in unstructured data such as documents and text, which helps prepare data for training or retrieval in AI systems. Integrations support popular databases and data warehouses, and subsetting tools cut large databases down to smaller, usable test sets.

item.title: Tulip
item.description:
Tulip brings software to the factory floor. Engineers and operators build apps using a drag-and-drop editor, with steps that guide workers through assembly, inspection, or maintenance, collect data, and trigger actions. Connecting sensors, machines, and tools lets the apps read real-time values, and the platform replaces clipboards and spreadsheets with digital work instructions and quality checks.

Analytics and automation extend the value. Dashboards show production performance, quality, and downtime, and machine learning models can detect anomalies or predict issues. Generative AI helps create apps from a description and analyze data in plain language. As a lightweight manufacturing execution system, it can be adopted gradually, line by line.

item.title: Uplight
item.description:
Uplight helps utilities communicate with customers and manage demand. It combines data on how households and businesses use energy with tools for personalized messages, home energy reports, smart thermostat programs, and marketplace offers for efficient appliances. The goal is to reduce peak demand and help customers cut bills, which lowers the need for expensive new capacity.

By acquiring AutoGrid, Uplight added software for managing distributed energy resources such as batteries, solar, EV chargers, and flexible loads. Together, the platform can enroll customers, control devices, and optimize their use as a virtual power plant, supported by machine learning for forecasting and targeting. It serves electric and gas utilities in many regions.

item.title: Vanta
item.description:
Vanta helps companies prove they run secure operations. It integrates with tools such as AWS, Google Workspace, GitHub, Okta, and HR systems, continuously checks whether controls like encryption, access reviews, and employee training are in place, and collects the evidence auditors need. This replaces manual screenshots and spreadsheets and keeps a company audit-ready year-round.

The platform has grown into a broader trust management suite. It tracks vendor risk, manages security policies and employee onboarding tasks, runs risk assessments, and provides a trust center where customers can see a company’s security posture. AI features answer security questionnaires, map controls across frameworks, and help prioritize remediation, saving time for small security teams.

item.title: Virtuous
item.description:
Virtuous aims to help nonprofits treat donors as individuals. Its CRM unifies donor records, giving history, communications, and activity from the website and email, and uses scoring to show which supporters are likely to give again or give more. Fundraisers use the data to plan outreach and prioritize relationships, rather than sending the same message to everyone.

Additional tools expand the system. Marketing automation builds journeys and email campaigns triggered by donor behavior, online giving forms and text-to-give accept gifts, and volunteer management tracks service. Newer AI features help write appeals, summarize donor histories, and recommend next steps for each supporter, and an analytics layer shows campaign performance.

item.title: 6sense
item.description:
6sense helps B2B teams find buyers who are not yet raising their hands. It collects signals from many sources, such as web visits, content consumption, and third-party research activity, identifies the companies behind the anonymous traffic, and uses machine learning to predict which accounts are in the market and at what stage of the buying journey. Teams see lists of target accounts ranked by readiness to buy.

The platform acts on those insights. Marketing can run advertising aimed at accounts showing interest, sales gets alerts when key accounts spike in activity, and workflows enroll contacts in email sequences. AI agents help with outreach and qualification, and integrations with CRMs and marketing automation tools keep data in sync. Predictions rely on data from many sources, so they are probabilistic.

item.title: ActiveCampaign AI
item.description:
ActiveCampaign is built around automation. You design customer journeys that react to behavior: someone joins a list, visits a page, abandons a cart, or opens an email, and the system sends the right follow-up at the right time. Segmentation, split testing, site tracking, and a built-in CRM let small and mid-sized businesses personalize campaigns without a large marketing team. It is common in e-commerce, services, and B2B companies.

Its AI tools help build and manage those journeys. Active Intelligence can audit an account, draft campaigns and automations from a short description, flag automations that are broken or underperforming, and answer questions about results in plain language. Predictive features estimate the best time to send, how likely a contact is to buy, and which deals are most likely to close. A content assistant writes subject lines and email copy.

item.title: Ada
item.description: Ada helps companies handle customer support questions without adding staff. Its AI agent answers inquiries on websites, in apps, and over messaging channels by drawing on a company’s knowledge base and systems, and it can take actions such as checking an order, changing an address, or processing a return by connecting to back-end tools. When a request is too complex or sensitive, it hands the conversation to a human agent with context.

item.title: Ada Health
item.description:
Ada guides users through a structured conversation about their symptoms. It asks about what you feel, when it started, your medical history, and related factors, adapting each question based on earlier answers, and then shows possible conditions with likelihoods and recommendations such as self-care, seeing a doctor, or seeking urgent help. The app was developed with doctors and is available in several languages.

The consumer app is free to use, and Ada also licenses its technology to health systems and insurers, who embed it in their own services for triage and navigation. The aim is to help people understand their symptoms, avoid unnecessary visits, and know when something needs prompt attention. Users can share a summary with their clinician.

item.title: AI21 Labs
item.description: AI21 Labs was founded by AI researchers in Tel Aviv and has been building language models since before ChatGPT made them mainstream. Its best-known models are the Jamba family, which blend a state-space architecture called Mamba with transformer layers. The aim is a model that handles very long documents with less memory and faster output than a standard transformer of similar size. Several Jamba versions have been released with open weights.

item.title: Airbyte
item.description: Airbyte solves the data movement problem. Data teams use it to pull information from applications, databases, and APIs, such as Salesforce, Postgres, Stripe, and Google Ads, and load it into destinations such as Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks, on a schedule. Hundreds of pre-built connectors cover common sources, and a low-code builder, with AI assistance, lets teams create connectors for others. Because it is open source, the connector catalog grows with community contributions.

item.title: Apollo
item.description:
Apollo gives sales teams a place to find and contact prospects. Users search a database of people and companies by title, industry, size, and technology used, then add leads to email sequences, calling lists, and LinkedIn tasks. A browser extension finds contact details as you browse the web.

The platform includes tools for the whole outbound workflow: email verification, scheduling, a dialer, meeting booking, analytics, and integrations with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot. AI features help write messages, score leads, and automate steps, and workflows can enrich existing records to keep a CRM current.

item.title: Apollo
item.description: Apollo is one of the most used tools for outbound sales. At its core is a searchable database of business contacts and companies, which you can filter by job title, industry, company size, location, technology used, and more. You export the matches or push them into sequences, and Apollo supplies emails and phone numbers. Startups and small sales teams like that it bundles data and outreach in one affordable product.

item.title: Attentive
item.description:
Attentive helps brands market over text message. Shoppers opt in through signup forms and popups, and the brand sends campaigns, product alerts, and automated messages such as abandoned cart reminders and back-in-stock notices. Messages can include images and links, and customers can reply to start a conversation.

AI plays a part in targeting and content. The platform chooses send times, predicts which offers each subscriber might respond to, and helps write messages in a brand’s voice. Integrations with Shopify, Klaviyo, and other tools bring in purchase data, and analytics tie messages to revenue. A service team often helps brands set up programs.

item.title: Avoma
item.description: Avoma joins sales, customer success, and recruiting meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then records and transcribes them and produces notes organized by meeting type. Instead of a generic summary, it uses templates suited to the call, such as a discovery call or a customer check-in, and pulls out action items, objections, and next steps. Notes and key fields can be pushed into CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot, which saves reps from doing data entry after every call.

item.title: Beatoven.ai
item.description: Beatoven.ai is aimed at video makers, podcasters, and game developers who need background music without searching a stock library. You describe the track you want, such as a calm acoustic piece for a travel vlog, or choose a genre, mood, and duration, and the AI composes an original piece. You can change the emotion of different sections along the timeline, which is helpful when a video moves from a tense moment to a resolved one.

item.title: BigCommerce
item.description:
BigCommerce provides the pieces needed to sell online. A merchant sets up a storefront with themes, manages products and inventory, accepts payments, calculates shipping and tax, and sells across channels such as Amazon, eBay, Google, social platforms, and marketplaces. Many features that other platforms handle through apps, such as product variants, reviews, and discounts, are built in, which keeps costs more predictable.

It stands out in two areas. It supports B2B commerce with features like customer-specific pricing, quotes, and bulk ordering, and it’s designed for headless setups in which the storefront is built separately and connected through APIs, which suits brands wanting a custom front end. AI tools help generate product descriptions, support merchandising, and optimize search, and an ecosystem of apps and partners extends the platform.

item.title: Blue Yonder
item.description: Blue Yonder helps companies plan and run their supply chains. Demand forecasting predicts what customers will buy, inventory planning decides how much stock to hold and where, and transportation and warehouse systems manage how goods move. Retailers, manufacturers, and logistics providers use it to balance supply and demand, reduce stockouts and excess inventory, and respond to disruptions. The company grew from JDA Software and acquired an AI startup that gave it its name.

item.title: Bubble
item.description:
Bubble lets people build real web apps without programming. The editor works by placing elements on a page, defining a database, and setting up workflows that say what happens when a user clicks or a condition occurs. Apps can include logins, payments, and integrations with other services.

It is used for marketplaces, internal tools, SaaS products, and prototypes, and some companies run substantial businesses on it. AI features can generate a starting app or page layout from a description, and plugins extend functionality. Bubble hosts the app, so there is no server to manage.

item.title: Bubble
item.description: Bubble lets people build real software without writing code. You design pages by dragging elements onto a canvas, define what happens when users click or submit with visual workflows, and store data in a built-in database. That is enough to build marketplaces, internal tools, customer portals, and SaaS products. Because the logic is visual but still detailed, Bubble apps can be quite complex, which is why it has been popular with founders who want to test an idea before hiring developers.

item.title: Capacity
item.description:
Capacity aims to be a single assistant across several support functions. It connects to a company’s knowledge sources and systems, then answers questions from employees about IT, HR, and policies, and from customers about products and orders. Automated workflows can complete actions such as resetting a password or opening a ticket.

The pitch is reducing the volume of tickets that require a person. By resolving common requests automatically and escalating the rest with context, it can free staff for harder issues. Analytics show which questions come up most and where documentation is lacking.

item.title: Casetext
item.description: Casetext began as a community site where lawyers annotated and shared case law, then grew into a legal research service with tools such as a brief-checking feature called Parallel Search, which found relevant cases using natural language. It was among the first legal technology companies to build on large language models, and its CoCounsel assistant could review documents, summarize depositions, draft research memos, and help prepare contract analyses with citations to sources.

item.title: Chatbase
item.description: Chatbase started as a simple way to create a chatbot from your own data. You upload files, point it to a website, or connect sources such as Notion, and it builds an agent that answers questions using that information. You embed the chat widget on your site with a snippet of code and you have support available around the clock. The simplicity made it popular with small businesses and startups that wanted a support bot without engineering work.

item.title: Civitai
item.description:
Civitai is where much of the open-source image generation community meets. Creators upload checkpoints, LoRAs, embeddings, and other add-ons for Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and related models, together with sample images and the prompts used. Others download them to run locally in tools like ComfyUI or Automatic1111, or try them in the browser. Ratings, comments, and example galleries make it easier to judge a model before downloading.

The site offers more than a library. Users can generate images on Civitai’s servers using credits, train their own LoRAs from a set of images, and take part in challenges and bounties that reward creators. Articles and guides share techniques, and a point system pays for the use of the site’s services. It became the unofficial catalog for community-trained styles, characters, and concepts.

item.title: ComfyUI
item.description: ComfyUI gives you precise control over generative AI by showing the whole pipeline. Instead of a prompt box and a button, you assemble a graph: load a model, encode a prompt, set up a sampler, add LoRAs or ControlNet for guidance, upscale, and save. Each step is a node you can inspect and rewire. It started with Stable Diffusion and now supports many image, video, and audio models, including FLUX, so new models are often usable in ComfyUI first.

item.title: Compass
item.description:
Compass is a brokerage that positions itself as a technology company. Its agents use a platform that combines a customer relationship manager, marketing tools for listings, market data, and transaction management in one place. Homebuyers and sellers use the site and app to search listings, see market trends, and work with an agent, and the tools are free to consumers because the company earns money through commissions on sales.

Technology supports the agent workflow. The platform helps with pricing recommendations, creates marketing materials such as brochures and social posts, tracks leads and client conversations, and organizes documents and deadlines through a deal. AI features assist with drafting listing descriptions, summarizing client interactions, and surfacing homes or clients to contact. The company has also tested private listings strategies for sellers.

item.title: Coursera
item.description:
Coursera partners with universities and companies to offer online learning at scale. Learners can take individual courses, follow multi-course specializations and professional certificates from names like Google, IBM, and Meta, or enroll in full online degrees. Material combines video lectures, readings, quizzes, and graded assignments, and many courses can be audited for free. Completed programs earn certificates that people add to resumes and LinkedIn.

AI has become part of the platform. A learning assistant answers questions about course content, gives feedback, and helps with practice, and tools help instructors and organizations build and translate courses faster. Skills-based recommendations suggest what to learn next based on your goals. The platform also offers business and government offerings, where employers assign programs and track progress.

item.title: Coze
item.description:
Coze lets non-programmers build conversational agents. In its editor, you describe the bot’s role and behavior, choose a language model, and attach tools: plugins for web search, image generation, and other services, plus knowledge bases that hold your documents. Visual workflows chain steps together for more complex tasks, and memory features let a bot recall details about users. A store lets creators share and discover bots built by others.

Publishing is flexible. A finished agent can be deployed to messaging apps and chat platforms, embedded on a website, or exposed through an API, which makes it practical for customer support, community bots, personal assistants, and internal tools. ByteDance has also released parts of the platform as open source for those who want to run it themselves, and offers separate editions for different regions.

item.title: Demandbase
item.description:
Demandbase focuses on selling to companies rather than individuals. It builds a view of target accounts from first-party and third-party data, including website visits, content use, and intent signals showing which accounts are researching a topic. Marketing and sales teams see which accounts are heating up and who within them is involved.

The platform acts on those signals. Advertising features serve targeted ads to the buying committee at chosen accounts, sales tools alert reps when accounts show interest, and orchestration coordinates campaigns across channels. AI helps score accounts, predict fit, and recommend actions, and an assistant answers questions about account data.

item.title: DocuSign AI
item.description:
Docusign made electronic signatures routine. Senders upload a document, specify signers and fields, and recipients sign on any device, with an audit trail and legal validity in many countries.
