It’s used for sales contracts, HR paperwork, real estate, and any agreement that once needed a pen, and it integrates with Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and many business systems.

The company has expanded to manage the whole agreement lifecycle. Its Intelligent Agreement Management platform includes tools to prepare and negotiate agreements, a repository that stores them, and AI that reads contracts to extract terms such as renewal dates, obligations, and parties. Its AI can summarize documents, answer questions about a contract portfolio, and flag risks, and workflow tools automate steps such as approvals and routing.

item.title: Dovetail
item.description:
Dovetail gives research teams a home for customer feedback. Researchers upload interviews and other data, and the platform transcribes recordings, lets them highlight key quotes, and organizes everything so insights can be found later. Teams build a searchable repository instead of losing findings in slide decks.

AI shortens the analysis step. It tags content automatically, groups related feedback into themes, summarizes sessions, and answers questions across a body of research. Reports and shareable highlights help researchers communicate with product teams and executives, and integrations pull in data from support and survey tools.

item.title: Duolingo
item.description:
Duolingo made language learning feel like a game. Lessons take a few minutes and mix translation, matching, listening, and speaking exercises. Streaks, experience points, and leagues reward consistency, and the friendly design and persistent reminders turned it into one of the most used education apps in the world. Courses cover languages from Spanish and French to Japanese, Korean, and smaller options, and it also offers math, music, and chess.

AI is a growing part of the product. A paid tier called Max includes features such as explanations of why an answer was right or wrong and role-play conversations with an AI character, and video call practice lets learners speak with an animated character. The company also uses AI to generate and personalize lesson content, which has been controversial among some users and staff who worry about quality and jobs.

item.title: Dynamic Yield
item.description:
Dynamic Yield helps businesses show each customer the content most likely to interest them. It collects behavior data from web, mobile, and email channels, builds profiles and segments, and uses machine learning to choose which products, banners, or messages to show. Retailers use it for recommendations like customers also bought, personalized homepages, and tailored promotions.

The platform also covers testing and optimization. Teams run experiments to compare versions of pages, with statistics to determine winners, and use triggers such as exit intent to present timely offers. Integrations connect with e-commerce platforms, customer data platforms, and marketing tools, and AI features suggest audiences and automate decisions. It supports use in industries including retail, travel, banking, and media.

item.title: ElevenLabs Sound Effects
item.description:
ElevenLabs Sound Effects creates audio from a sentence. You describe the sound you need, such as a door creaking in an empty house or a crowd cheering in a stadium, and the model generates several options in seconds, which you can adjust for length and download. This helps video editors, game developers, podcasters, and filmmakers who otherwise search libraries for the right clip or record effects themselves.

The company also offers a Voice Isolator that separates speech from background noise and music, helping clean up interviews and field recordings. These tools fit alongside ElevenLabs’ text-to-speech, dubbing, and music features, so a creator can produce a full soundtrack in one place. An API allows developers to generate effects inside apps and games.

item.title: Fashwell
item.description:
Fashwell works on a persistent problem in online retail: product data is often incomplete or inconsistent. Its AI looks at product photos and automatically identifies attributes such as category, color, pattern, shape, neckline, and material, creating detailed, standardized tags. Those tags help retailers organize catalogs, improve search, and power filters that match how customers describe items.

The same technology supports discovery features. Visual search lets shoppers find similar items from an image, recommendation systems suggest products that match a style, and outfit and style-matching tools help shoppers complete a look. Retailers use it to save the effort of manual tagging across thousands of items and to improve the consistency of information across channels.

item.title: Fireworks AI
item.description:
Fireworks AI focuses on serving open models efficiently. Developers call popular open-weight language, vision, image, and speech models through an API compatible with OpenAI’s format, and the platform’s optimized inference engine delivers low latency and high throughput. Many companies use it to run models at a lower cost than closed alternatives and to maintain control over which models they use.

The platform goes beyond hosting. It supports fine-tuning on a company’s data, including reinforcement learning methods, deploys custom models, and handles structured outputs and function calling for building agents. Dedicated deployments offer reserved capacity for steady workloads, and features such as batch processing reduce cost for non-urgent jobs. It runs in the cloud, with enterprise options for security and compliance.

item.title: Forethought AI
item.description: Forethought applies AI to the work that fills support queues. It reads incoming tickets and classifies them by topic and urgency, routes them to the right team, and drafts answers for human agents using the company’s knowledge base and past tickets. For common questions, its AI agents answer directly in chat and email and take simple actions such as checking an order status, handing off to a person when they cannot resolve the issue.

item.title: Foursquare
item.description:
Foursquare began as an app for checking in at places and discovering venues, but its main business today is location data. The company maintains a large database of points of interest, including businesses, landmarks, and venues, with details like categories, hours, and popularity. Developers use its Places API to add search, recommendations, and place information to maps and apps, and brands use its data to understand where people go.

Beyond place data, Foursquare provides tools for analyzing movement and location behavior. Panels of opted-in users allow measurement of foot traffic to stores, audience analysis, and attribution for advertising, and mapping and geospatial products let companies visualize and process location data at scale. Machine learning keeps place information up to date and helps match records from different sources.

item.title: Freshdesk
item.description: Freshdesk gives support teams a single place to handle customer requests. Messages from email, a web form, live chat, phone, and channels like WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram land in a shared inbox as tickets that can be assigned, tagged, prioritized, and tracked against service-level targets. A knowledge base lets customers find answers on their own, and a customer portal shows the status of their requests. It is used by companies from small startups to large support organizations.

item.title: Gemini Advanced
item.description:
Gemini Advanced was Google’s answer to ChatGPT Plus. When Google rebranded Bard as Gemini, it introduced Advanced as a subscription, sold through Google One, that gave access to its strongest model, longer conversations, and features like file uploads and integration with Gmail and Docs. It also bundled extra Google One storage, which made it attractive to people already paying for cloud storage.

Google later reorganized the plans. Gemini Advanced’s features moved into Google AI Pro, and a higher tier called Google AI Ultra provides the most advanced models, agent features, and generous limits for heavy users. The plans include perks such as video generation, deeper research tools, and integrations with Workspace apps, and the exact lineup changes with each product update.

item.title: GetIMG.ai
item.description: getimg.ai provides a web workspace for creating and editing images with AI. You can generate pictures from a prompt using a choice of models, including Stable Diffusion variants and other leading generators, then refine them. Tools for inpainting let you replace part of an image, outpainting extends it past its borders, and an infinite canvas allows you to compose scenes from several generations. Upscaling, background removal, and face tools help finish the result.

item.title: Gladly
item.description:
Gladly organizes support around the customer, not the ticket. Instead of separate cases for each channel, all interactions with a person appear in a single timeline, so an agent sees the entire history when a customer reaches out. That makes support feel more personal and reduces repeating information.

Sidekick is the AI part. It answers common questions, completes tasks like order lookups, and hands off to a human with context when needed. Assistive features summarize history and suggest replies. Gladly is used by consumer brands that care about the quality of service.

item.title: Glassdoor
item.description:
Glassdoor made workplace information public. Employees write anonymous reviews of their employers, covering culture, management, pay, and benefits, and share salary data and the questions they were asked in interviews. Job seekers use it to research a company before applying or accepting an offer, and to check whether an offer is in line with what others earn in similar roles.

The site also runs a job board and tools for employers. Companies can respond to reviews, post jobs, and promote their employer brand, while job seekers can search listings, set alerts, and apply. AI features appear in job recommendations and in summaries of reviews and salary information. Many of the platform’s operations have been merged with Indeed, its sister site, and Glassdoor is now legally part of Indeed, though the brand and reviews continue.

item.title: Gong
item.description:
Gong captures sales conversations and turns them into insight. It records calls and meetings, transcribes them, and pulls in emails and CRM data, then analyzes what is happening across the pipeline: which topics come up in deals that close, how often competitors are mentioned, how much reps talk compared with customers, and where deals are stalling. Managers can search a library of calls instead of relying on reps’ summaries.

The AI features save time at several levels. Calls are summarized with key points and next steps, which are written back to the CRM. Deal boards highlight risks, such as no recent contact with a decision-maker, and forecasting tools estimate which deals will close. Coaching tools find moments to review and compare behavior across reps, and newer AI agents help with tasks such as preparing for meetings, researching accounts, and drafting follow-ups.

item.title: Google Maps
item.description: Google Maps is the default map for much of the world. It provides turn-by-turn navigation with live traffic and rerouting, public transit schedules, walking and cycling directions, and detailed maps with business hours, photos, reviews, and popular times. Street View lets you look at places at ground level, Live View uses your phone’s camera to show directions as arrows in the real world, and offline maps work without a connection.

item.title: Gorgias
item.description:
Gorgias is a helpdesk made for online stores. Messages from email, live chat, social media, SMS, and phone arrive in one inbox, with the customer’s order history, shipping status, and account details shown next to the conversation. Agents can refund an order, edit an address, or cancel a shipment without leaving the ticket, which speeds up the most common support tasks in retail.

Automation takes care of a lot of the repetitive work. Rules route and tag tickets, macros fill in standard replies with order data, and self-service flows let shoppers track orders or request returns. An AI agent answers questions about shipping, returns, and products using the store’s policies and catalog, and can complete actions in the store before passing complex issues to people. Gorgias can also support sales conversations and product recommendations.

item.title: Groq
item.description: Groq is known for speed. Its chips, called Language Processing Units, were designed from scratch for running AI models rather than adapted from graphics hardware, and they produce text far faster than typical GPU-based services. That makes a difference for chat that feels instant, voice assistants that cannot afford to wait, and agents that make many model calls in a row. The company is not a model lab; it hosts models made by others.

item.title: Helpshift
item.description:
Helpshift places support inside the app. Users reach help from a screen in a game or mobile product, without leaving to email, and conversations carry context about the device, account, and recent activity. Agents see this information and respond in the same thread.

AI reduces the load. Intent detection reads messages, classifies the issue, and routes it to the right team, while chatbots answer common questions and collect details before a human steps in. A knowledge base and automation tools support self-service, and analytics track satisfaction and resolution times.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description: HubSpot started as a marketing software company and grew into a full platform for managing the customer relationship from first visit to renewal. It is organized into hubs: Marketing Hub for email, forms, ads, and landing pages, Sales Hub for pipelines and sequences, Service Hub for tickets and help desk, Content Hub for websites and blogs, and Operations Hub for data syncing and automation. All of them read from the same CRM, so a marketer, a sales rep, and a support agent are looking at one record of the customer.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description: HubSpot began as an inbound marketing tool, and Marketing Hub is still the center of its original idea: attract visitors with useful content, capture them as contacts, and nurture them toward a purchase. It includes email marketing, landing pages, forms, blogging, social publishing, ad tracking, and SEO recommendations, all tied to a CRM that records every interaction with a contact. That shared data is what lets a marketer see which campaigns produce actual customers, not only clicks.

item.title: HubSpot CRM
item.description: HubSpot CRM is the shared database underneath every HubSpot product, and it can also be used on its own at no cost. It stores contacts, companies, deals, and tickets, logs emails and calls against each record, and shows a pipeline of deals by stage. Connecting Gmail or Outlook means sent and received messages are attached to the right contact automatically, so people spend less time on manual data entry. For a small business that has been running on spreadsheets, it is an easy first step into a real CRM.

item.title: Intercom
item.description:
Intercom began as a live chat widget for websites and now covers the full range of customer communication. It combines a messenger on your site or app, a shared inbox for support teams, a searchable help center, email, and product tours. Companies use it to answer questions, onboard new users, and keep conversations in one thread across channels. It is common among software and subscription businesses.

Fin is the AI agent at the center of the current product. It reads your help articles and past conversations, then answers customer questions directly in chat and email, including follow-ups. When it cannot solve a problem or the customer asks for a person, it hands the conversation to a human with context attached. Fin can also take actions in other systems, like checking an order or updating an account, if you connect it. A copilot for human agents drafts replies and summarizes long threads.

item.title: Kasisto
item.description:
Kasisto builds AI assistants for banks. Its KAI technology understands banking questions and can carry out actions, such as showing recent transactions, transferring funds, or explaining a fee, in a chat within a bank’s mobile app or website. The language models are tuned to the vocabulary and rules of finance.

A newer product, KAI Answers, uses generative AI to answer questions from a bank’s own policies and documents, with citations so staff and customers can see the source. Banks use it to cut call volumes and improve self-service, and the company has worked with institutions around the world.

item.title: Krisp
item.description: Krisp installs as a virtual microphone and speaker, so it sits between your hardware and whatever calling app you use. It removes noise before it reaches the other person: barking dogs, keyboard clatter, traffic, and other voices in the room. It can also clean incoming audio, so a participant on a bad connection or in a loud space sounds clearer to you. Because it works with Zoom, Teams, Meet, Slack, and nearly any other app, one setup covers all of them.

item.title: Kustomer AI
item.description:
Kustomer takes a CRM-style approach to support. Instead of treating each ticket as an isolated item, it builds a timeline for each customer that includes every conversation, order, and interaction across channels. Agents see the full history in one view, which reduces the need to ask customers to repeat themselves. Channels include email, chat, SMS, social messaging, and voice, and workflow rules automate routing and tagging.

AI features have grown in importance. AI agents can answer common questions, check order status, and complete simple actions, escalating complex cases to humans with context. Tools for human agents summarize long histories, suggest replies, and classify issues, and insights analyze conversation patterns to find problems in products or processes. The system connects with e-commerce and business platforms to bring in order and account data.

item.title: Le Chat
item.description:
Le Chat is Mistral’s answer to ChatGPT and Claude. The French company designed the app for general use: answering questions, writing and editing, summarizing documents, analyzing images, generating images, and running code. Fast response modes make it quick for everyday queries, and a canvas supports working on documents and code beside the chat.

Further features address more advanced needs. Deep research compiles longer reports from web sources, connectors link to services like Gmail, Google Drive, and Notion, and custom agents let users set up specialized assistants. Memory can retain preferences between chats, and mobile apps bring it to phones. The assistant uses Mistral’s own models, some of which are open-weight, and emphasizes European hosting and privacy options.

item.title: LinkedIn
item.description:
LinkedIn is the main place for professional identity online. Members create profiles that work as living resumes, connect with colleagues and contacts, follow companies, and share posts and articles. It is also a major channel for hiring and job hunting, with job listings, recruiter messaging, and tools that show how you compare with other applicants. Companies maintain pages and advertise to professional audiences.

AI features run through the product. Job search can be done in plain language, writing assistance helps draft posts and profile sections, and an AI hiring assistant helps recruiters find and screen candidates. Premium subscriptions add insights, more messages, and learning courses through LinkedIn Learning. Skills assessments, recommendations, and endorsements are used to signal ability. The feed is ranked by algorithms that favor engagement.

item.title: LinkedIn Sales Navigator
item.description:
Sales Navigator gives salespeople deeper access to LinkedIn’s network. It provides advanced filters for finding people and companies, such as by seniority, function, company size, industry, and recent job changes. Users save leads and accounts into lists, and the system sends alerts when something relevant happens, like a prospect changing jobs or a company hiring in a certain department, which can prompt a timely message.

Further features support outreach. InMail messages reach people outside your network, TeamLink shows how colleagues are connected to a prospect for warm introductions, and integrations sync with CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot to keep records current. AI tools recommend leads, summarize accounts, and suggest ways to start a conversation, using the profile and activity data on the platform.

item.title: LM Studio
item.description:
LM Studio makes running models on your own computer approachable. You open the app, search a catalog of models from Hugging Face, download one that fits your hardware, and start chatting, with no command line needed. Everything runs locally, so conversations stay on your machine, you can work offline, and there are no per-token fees. It supports popular open models such as Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and gpt-oss.

For developers, LM Studio can start a local server that mimics the OpenAI API, so existing tools and scripts can point at your own model. It supports multiple model formats, including GGUF and Apple’s MLX for efficient performance on Mac, lets you tune settings such as context length and GPU offloading, and works with the Model Context Protocol to connect tools. A command-line version and SDKs support automation.

item.title: Loudly
item.description:
Loudly offers music for people who need soundtracks without composing. Users can create tracks by choosing a genre, mood, and tempo, or by describing what they want in a prompt, and then download the result. A library of ready-made AI tracks lets you browse by genre and use case. It is intended for video creators, podcasters, streamers, game developers, and businesses that need background music.

Several features support practical use. A personalization option adjusts elements like instruments and structure, stems can be downloaded for editing, and an API allows developers to embed music generation in their own products, such as apps that need adaptive soundtracks. The company positions its music as safe for commercial use, with licenses that cover content on social platforms.

item.title: Lovo AI
item.description:
Lovo makes synthetic speech for creators and businesses. Users type or paste a script, choose a voice, and adjust tone, speed, and emphasis to generate narration. Genny, the editor, lets them place speech alongside video, images, and music in one timeline.

Voice cloning and a marketplace of voices expand the options, and the platform supports many languages. Typical uses are explainer videos, e-learning, ads, and audiobooks. An API provides access for developers.

item.title: Magento
item.description:
Magento was created as an open-source e-commerce framework and became one of the most customizable platforms for online stores. Merchants with complex needs use it to manage large catalogs, multiple storefronts and currencies, custom pricing and checkout, and integrations with ERP and other systems. A huge ecosystem of extensions, agencies, and developers supports it.

Adobe acquired Magento and sells a commercial version, Adobe Commerce, with additional features for B2B selling, merchandising, and cloud hosting and support, plus integration with Adobe’s marketing and analytics products. Adobe Sensei AI powers features such as product recommendations and search. The free Magento Open Source edition continues for those who want to host and manage their own stores.

item.title: Microsoft Designer
item.description:
Microsoft Designer helps people make graphics quickly. You describe what you want, such as an invitation for a birthday party or a banner for a sale, and Designer produces several layout options with text, images, and styling, which you can edit. It offers templates for common formats, background removal, and tools for resizing a design for different platforms.

AI image generation is built in, powered by Microsoft’s and OpenAI’s image models, so you can create custom illustrations or photos to include in a design. It integrates with Microsoft 365 apps and Copilot, and is available on the web, as a mobile app, and inside tools such as Edge. Brand kits and shared templates are available on paid Microsoft 365 plans.

item.title: Microsoft Power Automate
item.description:
Power Automate connects apps and automates repetitive work. Users build flows that trigger on events, such as an email arriving or a form submission, and perform actions in hundreds of services. It works smoothly with Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, and Dynamics.

AI features extend it. Copilot lets people describe a flow in plain language, AI Builder processes documents and forms, and agent capabilities handle more open-ended tasks. Desktop flows use robotic process automation to control applications that have no API.

item.title: Microsoft Power Automate
item.description:
Power Automate helps people automate repetitive work without code. In a visual designer, users create flows that start from a trigger, such as an email arriving or a form being submitted, and then run actions like saving attachments, updating a spreadsheet, sending approvals, or posting to Teams. It connects to hundreds of services, with deep integration with SharePoint, Outlook, Excel, and Dynamics 365, and handles scheduled and event-driven tasks.

It also covers robotic process automation. Desktop flows record and replay actions on a computer, allowing automation of legacy applications that lack APIs. AI Builder adds capabilities such as reading text from documents, classifying content, and making predictions, and Copilot can build a flow from a plain-language description. Newer features support AI agents that use flows as tools.

item.title: Mixmax
item.description:
Mixmax turns Gmail into a sales workspace. It tracks opens, clicks, and replies, lets you schedule messages, and adds a calendar tool so recipients can book meetings from your email. Templates and snippets speed up repetitive writing, and polls, surveys, and documents can be embedded. It is used by sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that live in their inbox.

Sequences are a main feature: automated multi-step email campaigns that send follow-ups until someone replies, with rules for pausing and routing. Integrations connect with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach alternatives, Slack, and Zapier, so activity is logged in the CRM. AI helps draft emails, personalize at scale, and suggest next steps, and call recording and meeting notes have been added in some plans.

item.title: Monday.com
item.description:
Monday.com organizes work in colorful boards that resemble spreadsheets. Teams track projects, sales pipelines, marketing campaigns, and operations with columns for status, owners, dates, and more, and view the same data as a timeline, calendar, or chart. No-code automations handle routine updates and notifications.

The platform has expanded into products for sales CRM, service desks, and software development, built on the same foundation. AI assistants create boards from a description, summarize items and updates, write content, and extract information, and agents can take on tasks within workflows.

item.title: Moovly
item.description:
Moovly serves companies that need many versions of the same video. Using a template, teams can generate hundreds or thousands of variations that change names, products, languages, or data, such as personalized sales videos or product videos for each item in a catalog. A browser editor handles design, and an API automates production from spreadsheets or other systems.

Localization is a major theme. Moovly can add subtitles, translate scripts, and generate voiceovers in multiple languages using AI voices, helping companies serve international audiences, and AI tools assist with text-to-video and editing. It’s used in marketing, e-commerce, training, and communications, and offers brand controls and collaboration for large teams.

item.title: Netomi
item.description:
Netomi builds AI agents for customer support. Large brands connect it to their help desks and back-end systems, and the agents answer questions, track orders, process returns, and handle other requests across channels. Where an agent cannot resolve something, it hands off to a person with context.

The platform learns from past tickets and company content, and is built with controls such as guardrails and testing for regulated and high-volume environments. Customers include airlines, retailers, and travel companies that field heavy, repetitive inquiries.

item.title: Nosto
item.description:
Nosto helps online stores treat every visitor differently. It tracks browsing and purchase behavior and uses it to recommend products, order category pages, personalize search, and show targeted messages. Merchants configure these experiences with a visual tool and rules, and the system learns what works.

Features include product recommendations across the site and in emails, a search engine that understands intent, and tools to personalize content by audience. Shopify, Magento, and other platforms are supported. Generative AI helps write product copy and campaign content.

item.title: NotebookLM Plus
item.description: NotebookLM Plus gives heavier users more room in NotebookLM, Google’s tool for working with your own documents. The free version lets you add sources, ask questions with citations, and generate study aids, but it limits the number of notebooks, sources, and daily queries. The Plus tier lifts those limits, so people with large projects, such as researchers, students writing theses, or analysts working across many documents, can keep more material in one place.

item.title: Okendo
item.description:
Okendo helps online stores build trust with reviews. After a purchase, it asks customers for reviews with photos and video, displays them on product pages, and syndicates them to Google. Surveys and attributes gather more detail about the customer and product fit.

Additional tools include a loyalty and referral program and a customer data layer. AI summarizes reviews into themes, analyzes sentiment, and suggests replies, helping merchants learn what customers like and dislike. Integrations connect with email, helpdesk, and ads tools.

item.title: Paper Digest
item.description:
Paper Digest helps researchers keep up with a flood of new papers. Instead of scanning listings of new submissions every day, a user sets up topics or keywords and gets a personalized digest with short AI-generated summaries of matching papers. This helps researchers spot relevant work quickly and decide which papers merit a full read.

The service also publishes curated summaries of papers from major conferences and journals, and offers a platform to search, summarize, and organize papers. Paper Digest builds on text summarization models to produce abstracts and key points, and it provides tools such as a reader and a way to generate a quick literature overview. Some features are open to everyone, while others sit behind a login or subscription.

item.title: Personetics
item.description:
Personetics supplies the intelligence behind money management features in banking apps. Banks connect transaction data, and the platform generates timely, personalized messages and suggestions, like warning a customer that a bill will overdraw their account or noticing a good time to save.

The aim is a more engaging and useful banking relationship. Personetics works with large banks around the world and presents itself as a way to turn data into proactive guidance. AI generates the insights and chooses when and how to show them.

item.title: Quizlet AI
item.description:
Quizlet is a long-running tool for learning through flashcards. Students create or find sets of terms and definitions, then study them with modes such as flashcards, learn sessions that adapt to what you miss, matching games, and practice tests. A huge library of user-created sets covers school subjects, languages, and professional exams, and teachers use it to build class activities.

AI has added help with creating and understanding material. Tools can generate flashcards or quizzes from uploaded notes, textbook pages, or slides, saving the effort of typing each card. An AI tutor can explain a concept, quiz you, and give step-by-step help, and features track progress and suggest what to review. Study guides and summaries can be produced from your own materials.

item.title: Raycast AI
item.description:
Raycast puts a command bar on your keyboard. Press a hotkey, type a few letters, and you can launch apps, search files, run calculations, manage windows, paste snippets, control music, and use hundreds of extensions that connect to tools such as GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Slack. Power users value how much it can cut mouse use and context switching.

Raycast AI adds chat and commands powered by leading language models. You can ask a question, rewrite selected text, summarize a page, translate, or run custom AI commands from any app, and switch among models from different providers. AI Extensions let the assistant act through extensions, such as creating an issue or checking a calendar, and Model Context Protocol support connects it to more tools. Chats and presets are synced across devices.

item.title: Recharge
item.description:
Recharge enables subscribe-and-save models for online stores. Merchants on Shopify and other platforms set up subscription products, let customers manage deliveries and payments in a portal, and bill on schedule. It is common in consumables such as food, supplements, and beauty products.

Analytics show retention, churn, and revenue, and tools help reduce cancellations. Smart payment retries recover failed charges, and AI models predict which subscribers may leave so merchants can intervene with offers or pauses.

item.title: Redfin
item.description:
Redfin helped modernize home search. Its site and app show listings with details, photos, and maps, along with estimated home values, price history, and tools to compare neighborhoods. A key difference from traditional brokerages is that its agents are salaried employees instead of paid mostly on commission, and Redfin has competed on lower listing fees and a customer-focused model.

Technology plays a large role. Its valuation model, the Redfin Estimate, uses machine learning on recent sales and listing data to estimate home values, and tools offer alerts, tours scheduling, and offers online. AI features help with search and recommendations. Rocket Companies, the owner of Rocket Mortgage, acquired Redfin, bringing mortgage and agent services together under a combined offering, including financing incentives when buyers use both.

item.title: Replika
item.description: Replika is one of the earliest AI companion apps. You create an avatar, choose a name and appearance, and begin chatting. Over time the AI builds a memory of your interests, relationships, and preferences, and the avatar responds in a way that reflects that history. Users talk to it about their day, vent about problems, practice conversations, or just keep company. It offers text chat, voice calls, and an augmented reality mode that places the avatar in your room.

item.title: Rippling
item.description:
Rippling combines employee data with the systems that depend on it. When a person joins, Rippling creates their payroll record, sets up benefits, provisions laptops and software accounts, and orders equipment, using one source of truth. Changes in the employee record cascade across the systems.

Modules cover HR, payroll in many countries, time and attendance, benefits, device and app management, and corporate cards and expenses. A workflow engine lets admins automate approvals and tasks, and AI assistants answer questions and draft content.

item.title: Salesforce
item.description: Salesforce is the CRM that large companies tend to run their sales and customer operations on. It tracks leads, accounts, opportunities, and support cases, and it is sold as separate clouds for Sales, Service, Marketing, and Commerce, with Slack, Tableau, and MuleSoft added for collaboration, analytics, and integration. Underneath is a platform that lets companies build custom objects, workflows, and apps, which is why Salesforce setups can look very different from one company to the next.

item.title: Salesforce Einstein
item.description:
Einstein brought AI to Salesforce customers well before generative AI became popular. Predictive features score leads and opportunities, forecast revenue, recommend next best actions, and flag at-risk accounts, using each company’s own CRM data. Einstein Discovery finds patterns and suggests what drives outcomes, and bots and analytics features extend the same ideas to service and marketing.

With generative AI, Einstein has expanded to write emails, summarize records and cases, and generate service replies, grounded in customer data and protected by the Einstein Trust Layer, which masks sensitive information and prevents customer data from being used to train outside models. The conversational assistant evolved into Agentforce, which builds autonomous agents on the same foundation, so Einstein now refers to a mix of older predictive features and the generative AI infrastructure.

item.title: SalesLoft
item.description:
Salesloft helps sales teams organize outbound and follow-up work. Reps follow cadences, which are structured sequences of emails, calls, and social touches, and the platform tells them who to contact next and records each activity in the CRM. Managers can see which messages and sequences generate replies and meetings, and coach reps with call recordings and analytics.

The platform has expanded into revenue orchestration. Conversation intelligence records and summarizes calls, deal management tracks stage progress and risk, and forecasting tools combine pipeline data with engagement signals. Salesloft acquired Drift for conversational marketing and has combined with Clari, a revenue forecasting company, to build a broader revenue platform. AI assistants prepare meeting briefs, draft messages, and suggest next steps.

item.title: Scale AI
item.description:
Scale AI built its business on a simple observation: AI models need huge amounts of well-labeled data, and quality control at scale is hard. It combines software with a large network of human contributors and experts to annotate images, video, text, and sensor data. Early customers included self-driving car developers, and the company grew by supplying training data to the biggest AI labs.

Today much of its work involves large language models. Scale provides human feedback data used in reinforcement learning, expert-written examples for fine-tuning, and evaluations that test models for accuracy and safety. Its tools help companies manage data pipelines, and a generative AI platform lets enterprises customize models on their own data. Public-sector work includes AI systems for defense and government agencies, and the company runs public leaderboards that rank models on hard tests.

item.title: Scenario
item.description:
Scenario is built around consistency, which is the main challenge of using generative AI in game production. A studio uploads examples of its art, and Scenario trains a custom model that learns the style, so the characters, props, and environments it generates look like they belong in the same game. Artists can use it to create concepts, variations, and finished assets faster.

The platform covers more than still images. It can generate sprites, textures, icons, and UI elements, create variations of existing pieces, convert images into 3D models, and offers workflows for upscaling and cleaning outputs. An API and plugins connect it to game engines and pipelines, and team features support collaboration and asset management. The focus is on production use by studios and indie developers.

item.title: Semgrep
item.description:
Semgrep scans code for patterns. Rules look like the code they match, which makes them easier to write than traditional analyzers’ queries. Teams use community rules for common vulnerabilities and write custom ones for their own standards, running scans in CI and on developers’ machines.

The commercial platform adds dependency scanning, secrets detection, and a triage assistant that uses AI to explain findings, suggest fixes, and filter likely false positives. It integrates with pull requests and issue trackers.

item.title: ServiceNow
item.description:
ServiceNow began as an IT service management tool and became a general workflow platform for large organizations. Employees and customers submit requests, such as a laptop problem, a payroll question, or a customer complaint, and the platform routes, tracks, and resolves them using defined workflows. Companies use it as a system of record and action across IT operations, HR, legal, security, and customer service.

AI is central to its current strategy. Now Assist adds generative AI to summarize cases, draft replies, and help agents find answers, and AI agents can take on tasks such as triaging incidents and fulfilling requests with minimal human intervention. The company acquired Moveworks, whose employee assistant is intended to become the front door to the platform, and offers tools to govern and monitor agents across the enterprise.

item.title: Shopify
item.description: Shopify lets someone start an online store without building the software behind it. You choose a theme, add products, set up payments and shipping, and the platform handles hosting, the checkout, and tax and currency settings. The same system also covers in-person sales through point-of-sale hardware, so a shop can manage online and physical inventory together. Everything from a one-person side business to large brands runs on it, and Shop Pay, its accelerated checkout, is used well beyond Shopify’s own stores.

item.title: SideChef
item.description:
SideChef is built for people who want help in the kitchen. Each recipe is broken into short steps with photos or video, so you can follow along while cooking, and hands-free voice control and timers keep you moving without touching your phone with messy hands. Recipes cover a wide range of cuisines and diets, and you can scale servings, swap ingredients, and save favorites.

Planning features reduce the work around cooking. Meal plans suggest weekly menus based on tastes and dietary needs, and shopping lists are built automatically from chosen recipes, with options to order groceries through delivery partners. The app also works with smart kitchen devices, and AI helps personalize recommendations and adjust plans over time.

item.title: SimilarWeb
item.description:
Similarweb lets you look at the performance of sites you do not own. Enter a domain, and it shows estimated monthly visits, traffic sources such as search, social, and direct, top keywords, referring sites, audience demographics, and engagement metrics like time on site. Data comes from a mix of panels, partnerships, and public sources, modeled to produce estimates. This helps in benchmarking competitors and finding growth opportunities.

The platform covers more than websites. It tracks app usage and downloads, advertising, and market segments, and ranks sites within categories. Recent additions include tracking how brands and sites are cited and visited through AI chatbots, reflecting the way people increasingly use AI assistants instead of search. Investors use the data to spot trends in company performance before financial reports, and sales teams use it to find leads.

item.title: Softr
item.description:
Softr turns data into software. A user connects Airtable, Google Sheets, or its own database, and builds pages with blocks such as lists, forms, dashboards, and charts. Logins and permissions control which users see which records.

Typical products include client portals, directories, simple CRMs, and internal tools. The AI builder creates an app from a description, and workflows automate actions. Hosting and a custom domain are included.

Softr has a free plan and paid tiers by users and features. Complex logic is limited compared with full code. Alternatives include Glide, Pory, Stacker, Bubble, and Retool. Softr suits non-developers building apps on spreadsheets and databases.

item.title: Stamped.io
item.description:
Stamped helps online stores build trust. After a purchase, it emails customers asking for reviews, collects star ratings with photos or videos, and displays them on product pages and in search results with structured data. Social proof improves conversion rates, and review requests can be automated and timed, with options to send coupons for leaving a review.

The platform also offers loyalty and referral programs. Customers earn points for purchases and actions, redeem rewards, and refer friends, which encourages repeat business. AI features summarize reviews into key themes, surface what customers love or dislike, and help merchants respond. Reports show review volume, ratings, and the effect on sales, and integrations connect with email, helpdesk, and ads tools.

item.title: Stitch Fix
item.description:
Stitch Fix popularized personal styling by mail. A client fills out a style profile, and a stylist assisted by algorithms selects pieces, ships them in a box, and the client keeps what they like and returns the rest. Feedback improves later selections.

Data science is central to the company. Algorithms analyze preferences, item attributes, and inventory to predict what each customer will like, while stylists add judgment. Generative AI tools support outfit suggestions and visual try-on, and customers can also shop directly.

item.title: StockImg AI
item.description:
StockImg AI turns a description into a usable image. Instead of searching a stock library for something close to what you imagine, you type what you want and the tool creates it. It offers separate generators geared to common needs: logo designs, ebook and book covers, posters, wallpapers, illustrations, and app screen mockups. Each has settings suited to its format, such as aspect ratios for covers and posters.

The tool also includes editing functions. You can adjust and regenerate images, remove backgrounds, and explore variations. Self-publishers, small businesses, bloggers, and social media managers use it to get covers and graphics without hiring a designer or paying for licenses. The output is meant to be unique to your prompt, which avoids the problem of the same stock photo showing up in many places.

item.title: SubtitleBee
item.description:
SubtitleBee automates subtitles. You upload a video, choose the spoken language, and the tool transcribes it and creates timed captions, which you can edit in a simple editor. It supports many languages and can translate subtitles into others, helping creators reach international audiences. Typical users are YouTubers, social media managers, educators, and marketers, who need captions because many viewers watch with the sound off.

Style options let captions fit a brand: you can change fonts, colors, positions, and highlight words as they are spoken, which is a popular look on short-form video. Subtitles can be exported as files for use in other editors or burned into the video itself. Plans are tied to the amount of video processed, and the product is in a crowded category.

item.title: Supernormal
item.description:
Supernormal aims to make meeting notes require no effort. A bot joins your scheduled meetings, records and transcribes them, and creates notes organized by templates for different types of meetings, such as sales calls, interviews, one-on-ones, and standups. The notes list decisions, action items, and key points, and are shared with attendees or saved to the tools your team uses.

The product works across platforms, including Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, and also supports in-person meetings. Integrations push notes to Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce, and Google Docs. Search and chat features let you look back at past meetings and ask questions, and customization options allow you to adjust the format of the notes.

item.title: Tana
item.description:
Tana combines outlining with databases. Everything is a node in an outline, and tagging a node with a Supertag gives it fields and behavior, so a note about a person, a book, or a project becomes structured and can be queried and viewed in many ways. Backlinks connect related ideas.

AI is integrated into the workflow. It can transcribe meetings and turn them into tagged notes, fill in fields, and answer questions across a workspace, and it can act on commands users define. Voice capture makes it easy to record ideas on the go.

item.title: Tempus AI
item.description:
Tempus builds a bridge between lab results and clinical decisions. It sequences tumors and other samples, combines the results with clinical data, and provides physicians with reports to help guide treatment choices, such as matching patients to targeted therapies or clinical trials. Over time, the company has assembled a large library of linked clinical and molecular data.

That data supports a second business: working with pharmaceutical companies. Tempus licenses de-identified data and builds models to help discover and develop drugs, find suitable patients for trials, and analyze outcomes. It has expanded through acquisitions into digital pathology with Paige and into radiology with the former Arterys platform, aiming to combine images, genomics, and clinical records into foundation models.

item.title: tl;dv
item.description:
tl;dv, short for “too long; didn’t view,” saves people from rewatching meetings. A bot joins your calls to record and transcribe them in many languages, and you can mark highlights during the call. Afterward, the recording is available with an AI-generated summary and a list of action items, plus timestamps so you can jump to the part that matters. Clips can be shared with people who missed the meeting.

The tool is popular with sales and product teams. It can fill in CRM fields in tools like HubSpot and Salesforce, produce reports across many meetings to spot patterns such as customer objections, and send notes to Slack and Notion. Templates tailor summaries to sales calls, user interviews, and team meetings, and search lets you find topics across your library.

item.title: Udemy
item.description:
Udemy opened online teaching to anyone. Instructors create video courses on a huge range of topics, from Python programming and UX design to photography and personal finance, and learners buy them individually, often at steep discounts. Courses can be watched at your own pace for life, and ratings and reviews help buyers choose. Quality varies widely, as there is little gatekeeping.

For companies, Udemy Business provides a curated library of courses with analytics and learning paths, which many organizations use for employee training. AI features include assistants that answer questions about course content, recommend lessons, and help instructors build courses, and role-play practice tools for skills training. Udemy has emphasized AI and technology skills, which are among its most popular categories.

item.title: Vapi
item.description:
Vapi handles the hard parts of voice agents. Developers define an assistant with a prompt and tools, connect a phone number, and Vapi orchestrates speech-to-text, the language model, and text-to-speech, with handling for interruptions and turn-taking. Bring-your-own provider choices allow swapping components.

Use cases include customer support lines, appointment scheduling, outbound calls, and voice assistants in apps. The platform includes testing, analytics, and call transfer features.

Vapi is billed by minutes plus provider costs. Voice calls are regulated, and callers should know they are speaking with an AI. Alternatives include Retell AI, Bland AI, Synthflow, Twilio ConversationRelay, and LiveKit. Vapi suits developers building voice agents.

item.title: Voicemod
item.description: Voicemod changes how you sound as you speak. You choose a voice effect, such as a robot, a deep voice, or a character, and the app processes your microphone audio in real time. It works as a virtual microphone, so apps like Discord, Zoom, OBS, and many games treat it like a normal mic. Gamers and streamers use it for fun and for roleplay, and some people use it for privacy.

item.title: Vue.ai
item.description:
Vue.ai is built for retailers with large catalogs. Computer vision reads product images and assigns attributes such as color, pattern, neckline, fabric, and occasion, which saves teams from tagging thousands of items by hand. Those tags feed search, filters, and merchandising, so shoppers find items that match what they want.

The same data drives the customer-facing side. Recommendation engines suggest items based on browsing and purchase behavior, visual search lets shoppers upload a photo to find similar products, and styling tools suggest outfits that go together. Merchandisers can also see how products perform and adjust collections and layouts.

item.title: WellSaid Labs
item.description:
WellSaid focuses on voiceovers for businesses. In its web studio, you type or paste a script, pick a voice, and generate narration with control over pacing, pronunciation, and emphasis. The voices are built from recordings by professional voice actors who agreed to the use, which gives companies a clear license position. Typical projects include training courses, explainer videos, product tours, corporate announcements, and audio for apps.

For larger teams, collaboration and control matter. Projects can be shared, commented on, and reviewed, and custom pronunciation settings keep brand names and technical terms consistent across a library of content. An API lets developers add speech to their own products, and integrations connect WellSaid to e-learning and creative tools. Enterprise plans emphasize security, privacy, and compliance, and custom voices can be created for a brand.

item.title: Whisk
item.description:
Whisk started as an independent app for collecting recipes. You could save dishes from any food site into one library, group them into collections, plan meals for the week, and turn the ingredients into a shopping list that could be sent to grocery delivery services. A browser extension made saving a recipe a single click.

Samsung bought the company and renamed the app Samsung Food, and the whisk.com address now leads to the new brand. The app keeps the same core features and adds AI help, such as adjusting a recipe to dietary needs, suggesting meals from what you have, and generating plans. It also connects with Samsung’s smart appliances, though it works without them on phones and the web.

item.title: Wix ADI
item.description:
Wix ADI, short for Artificial Design Intelligence, was an early attempt at automatic site building. A user answered questions about their business and style, and ADI generated a layout with text, images, and a structure suited to the industry. It let people with no design skills get a website online in minutes, long before generative AI was common.

ADI sites had limits. They used a simpler editor than the main Wix Editor, which made it hard to customize them or to add advanced features. Wix has since retired the product: ADI sites are no longer supported and existing ones were moved into the standard Wix Editor, so owners can keep editing them there.

item.title: WooCommerce
item.description:
WooCommerce is the most widely used way to run a store on WordPress. You install the plugin, add products, set up payments, shipping, and taxes, and manage orders from the WordPress dashboard. Because it is open source, you own the store and the data, host it where you want, and can modify anything with code or extensions.

The ecosystem is its strength. Thousands of themes and extensions add subscriptions, bookings, memberships, marketplaces, and connections to accounting and marketing tools. AI extensions can write product descriptions, suggest recommendations, and help with support, and Automattic’s own tools plus third-party plugins fill the gaps. Many agencies build custom stores on top of it.

item.title: Wordsmith
item.description:
Wordsmith turns data into text. Users define templates and logic, connect a data source, and the platform writes a narrative for each record, such as a financial summary, a sports recap, or a personalized report. The output is consistent and can be produced in volume.

It predates today’s chat models. Rule-based natural language generation gives predictable text, which suits regulated reporting where exact control matters, while large language models offer flexibility and fluency but less predictability.

item.title: Writerly
item.description:
Writerly is aimed at teams that want AI-written content to sound like them. Instead of generating generic text, it lets users supply samples of their existing writing and style guidelines, then drafts articles, emails, and social posts that follow that voice. That approach is common among brand-focused writing tools, and matters most for companies with several writers.

Features reported in directories include templates for common content types, collaboration for editors and reviewers, and options to reuse past content. Teams often use this kind of tool to keep messaging consistent across channels and to speed up first drafts, with humans editing for accuracy and judgment.

item.title: Yelp
item.description:
Yelp built its business on reviews. Users write about their experiences with restaurants, home services, medical offices, and other local businesses, rate them, and upload photos. Search results combine ratings, distance, price, and filters such as open now or takeout, which helps people choose. In the United States, it is a major source for restaurant and service recommendations.

Businesses can claim their listing, add information, respond to reviews, and run ads, and some features support booking, waitlists, and requesting quotes from local professionals. AI has been added to the product: assistants help users find places through conversation, summaries condense long review histories, and tools detect and filter spam and fake reviews through a recommendation software that sorts reviews by reliability.

item.title: Yotpo
item.description:
Yotpo helps online stores build trust and repeat business. It collects reviews with photos, shows them on product pages and in search, and runs loyalty programs and referral offers. SMS and email tools extend marketing.

AI summarizes reviews into themes, flags issues, and drafts responses, and analytics tie content to conversion. Integrations cover Shopify, BigCommerce, and other platforms.

Yotpo has a free tier and paid plans that scale with orders. Alternatives include Okendo, Judge.me, Stamped.io, Klaviyo, and Trustpilot. Yotpo suits growing online stores.

item.title: Zendesk
item.description:
Zendesk is one of the most widely used help desk systems. Customer messages from email, web chat, phone, WhatsApp, and social media become tickets in a shared workspace, where they can be routed, prioritized, and tracked against service targets. A help center and community forum let customers find answers themselves, and reports show response times and satisfaction. It scales from small support teams to large contact centers.

The current product is built around AI. AI agents take on requests from start to finish, answering from help articles and past conversations, and taking actions in connected systems when allowed. A copilot assists human agents by suggesting replies, summarizing long threads, and flagging urgent or unhappy customers. The platform has added contact center, workforce management, and quality assurance tools, and an employee service product that applies the same ideas to internal IT and HR requests.

item.title: Zowie
item.description:
Zowie focuses on online retail support. Its AI agent connects to a store’s order system, answers questions about delivery and returns, processes simple actions, and hands off tricky cases to staff. It works across chat, email, and messaging channels.

The platform emphasizes decision-making that follows a brand’s policies, and gives support managers tools to review and adjust behavior. Analytics show resolution rates and topics.

Zowie is sold on subscription. Alternatives include Gorgias, Intercom Fin, Ada, Netomi, and Zendesk AI agents. Zowie suits e-commerce support teams.

item.title: Aisera
item.description: Aisera provides AI agents for internal and external service desks. Employees can ask for help with IT issues, such as resetting a password or requesting software, or HR questions, such as time off policies, and the agent resolves the request by taking actions in connected systems instead of simply pointing to articles. For customers, similar agents handle support inquiries. The goal is to reduce the number of tickets that reach human staff.

item.title: Artisan AI
item.description:
Artisan describes its products as autonomous teammates rather than assistants. Ava, the AI BDR, works through the outbound sales process: building a list of prospects from a database, researching each, writing personalized messages, sending them, and handling follow-up. The company aims mainly at startups and small teams that cannot hire a full sales development group.

Ava connects to a company’s email, CRM, and calendar, and can book meetings that appear for human salespeople. The company also talks about expanding to other roles. Automation can increase outreach volume, but results depend on how well the target list and message match the market.

item.title: Ashby
item.description:
Ashby brings together tools that recruiting teams often buy separately. The core is an applicant tracking system for jobs, candidates, and interview plans. Around it sit scheduling that coordinates interviewers automatically, a CRM for sourcing and nurturing talent, and an analytics layer that shows pipeline health, time to hire, and source effectiveness.

AI features handle repetitive work, such as summarizing candidates, drafting outreach, and taking notes in interviews. Structured scorecards and interview plans promote consistent evaluation, and reporting is built into the product rather than added on, which analytics-minded recruiting teams like.

item.title: Attio
item.description:
Attio starts from the idea that every company sells differently. Instead of fixed objects like leads and opportunities, teams build their own structures, such as customers, partners, or investors, and link them. The interface feels more like a spreadsheet and a database than a traditional CRM, so it is easier to reshape.

Data fills in with little typing. Attio connects to email and calendar to log interactions, enriches company and contact details, and shows the strength of relationships. AI features summarize accounts, answer questions about the pipeline, and fill in fields from conversations. Workflow automation moves records, sends notifications, and updates data.

item.title: Bloomreach
item.description:
Bloomreach serves online retailers. Its discovery product powers site search, category pages, and recommendations, using machine learning to understand what shoppers mean, rank products, and personalize results. Merchandisers can set rules and see how changes affect sales.

The platform also includes engagement tools. A customer data platform unifies behavior across channels, and marketing automation sends email, SMS, and push messages triggered by actions. Content management supports headless sites. AI assistants help marketers build campaigns and analyze performance.

item.title: Botpress
item.description: Botpress started as an open-source tool for building chatbots with visual flows, and it grew into a platform around large language models. Developers and technical teams build agents that talk with customers on websites and messaging channels, connect to knowledge bases, and call APIs to do things like check an order or update an account. A visual builder and code options sit side by side, so non-engineers can adjust conversations while developers handle integrations.

item.title: Braze
item.description:
Braze helps brands talk to customers on the channels where they spend time. Marketers segment users by behavior, design journeys in a visual canvas, and send messages triggered by actions such as opening an app, abandoning a cart, or reaching a milestone. Real-time data means messages respond to what is happening now.

AI features improve targeting and creation. Predictive models estimate who might churn or buy, optimization chooses the best send time and channel for each person, and generative tools help write subject lines and copy. Analytics measure the effect of campaigns on retention and revenue.

item.title: Cassidy AI
item.description:
Cassidy lets non-technical teams build AI workflows. A user connects sources such as documents, wikis, and apps, then designs assistants and multi-step workflows in a visual builder: take an input, retrieve company knowledge, draft an output, and send it onward.

Typical uses include drafting proposals and emails in the company’s voice, summarizing meetings, researching accounts, answering internal questions, and processing forms. Different model providers can be used, and permissions control who can see which sources. Teams share assistants so a good workflow becomes a reusable tool.

item.title: CleverTap
item.description:
CleverTap serves brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavioral data such as app opens, purchases, and feature use, builds segments, and lets marketers send push notifications, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and in-app messages. Journeys can be designed visually so that actions trigger the next message.

AI is used for prediction and optimization. Models estimate which users are likely to churn or convert, choose the best time and channel for each message, and recommend products. A proprietary database designed for large volumes of event data keeps analysis fast, and analytics show retention, funnels, and campaign results.

item.title: Codecademy
item.description:
Codecademy teaches coding by doing. Lessons present a short explanation beside an editor where learners write code and see results right away, which makes it approachable for beginners. Courses cover languages such as Python, JavaScript, and SQL, as well as web development, data analysis, and machine learning.

Career paths and skill paths structure the learning, with projects and quizzes to check progress. An AI assistant helps learners who are stuck by giving hints and explaining errors, while avoiding simply handing over answers. Business plans let companies train teams, and Skillsoft acquired Codecademy to add it to its corporate learning catalog.

item.title: ContractPodAi
item.description:
ContractPodAi was built for corporate legal departments that handle large volumes of contracts. Its platform covers the lifecycle: drafting from templates, routing for approval, negotiation, signature, storage in a searchable repository, and tracking of obligations and renewals. It connects with systems such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and ERP tools so contracts sit within the business processes they relate to.

The company has rebranded as Leah, after the name of its AI product, and now describes itself as an agentic AI platform. Its AI agents review contracts against playbooks, flag risks and deviations, extract key terms, answer questions about a contract portfolio, and handle repetitive tasks across legal, procurement, and finance. The change reflects a wider move in legal technology from software that stores documents to software that does the first pass of the work.

item.title: CSM AI
item.description:
CSM turns simple inputs into 3D assets. A user uploads a picture, types a description, or draws a sketch, and the system produces a 3D model with textures that can be exported to common formats. It supports game developers, designers, and creators who need assets quickly.

Beyond single objects, it offers tools for character creation and animation preparation, and an API lets developers build 3D generation into their own apps. The output is often a starting point that artists clean up, since generated meshes can have topology problems that matter for animation and games.

item.title: Docsumo
item.description:
Docsumo turns documents into structured data. A company uploads or emails PDFs and scans such as invoices, receipts, bank statements, and forms, and the platform reads fields and tables, checks them against rules, and sends clean data to accounting, lending, or ERP systems. This replaces manual entry.

A review interface lets staff correct uncertain fields, and corrections improve accuracy over time. Pre-trained models cover common documents, while custom models handle company-specific layouts. Workflows include validation rules, approvals, and integrations through APIs. Lenders and finance teams are major users.

item.title: Dust
item.description:
Dust helps companies deploy AI assistants on their own information. Administrators connect sources such as Notion, Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, and Confluence, and create assistants for functions like support, sales, or engineering. Each assistant has instructions and access to selected data, so answers are grounded in the company’s content.

Employees use assistants in a chat interface or inside Slack, and assistants can take actions through connected tools. Teams share assistants they build, so a good one becomes common property. The platform works with models from several providers, and focuses on security and permissions.

item.title: Folk
item.description:
Folk is a relationship manager for people who find traditional CRMs heavy. Users import contacts from email, LinkedIn, and spreadsheets, organize them into groups, and track conversations and deals in a clean interface. It suits agencies, recruiters, investors, and founders who manage many relationships.

AI and automation reduce the manual work. Enrichment fills in details like company and role, a browser extension saves profiles from LinkedIn, and sequences send personalized emails at scale. AI helps write messages and summarize history, and reminders prompt follow-ups so nobody falls through the cracks.

item.title: Front
item.description:
Front treats shared inboxes like collaborative workspaces. Support, sales, and account teams manage messages from several channels in one place, assign conversations, leave internal comments, and see who is handling what. The interface resembles email, so adoption is easy.

Automation and AI reduce manual work. Rules route messages, tag them, and set priorities, while AI summarizes long threads, suggests replies, and answers common questions. Analytics show response times and workloads, and integrations with CRMs and helpdesk tools provide context.

item.title: Insider
item.description:
Insider helps brands treat each visitor differently. It collects behavior data across channels, builds unified profiles, and uses them to personalize websites, app experiences, and messages. A marketer can design a journey that reaches a customer by email, then push, then SMS depending on what they do.

The AI layer predicts what people are likely to buy or whether they may churn, recommends products, and optimizes timing and content. The platform also includes tools for search, recommendations, and conversational commerce. It is used heavily by retailers and consumer brands in many regions.

item.title: Iterable
item.description:
Iterable lets marketers build cross-channel journeys. They segment customers by behavior, design workflows in a visual canvas, and send messages triggered by actions, such as signing up, abandoning a cart, or reaching a milestone. Data from websites, apps, and warehouses feeds the profile used for personalization.

AI assists in several areas: optimizing the time a message is sent for each person, predicting engagement, recommending content, and helping generate copy. Experimentation tools test variants, and analytics tie campaigns to outcomes. Integration with data warehouses supports teams that centralize customer data.

item.title: Klevu
item.description:
Klevu improves how online shoppers find products. Instead of matching keywords exactly, its search engine uses natural language processing to interpret queries, handle synonyms and misspellings, and rank results based on relevance and merchandising goals. It works with platforms such as Shopify, Magento, and BigCommerce.

The product also includes category browsing, recommendations, and analytics on what shoppers search for and fail to find. Merchandisers can adjust results with rules, and AI personalization adapts to a shopper’s behavior. A chat-style assistant answers product questions.

item.title: Lummi
item.description:
Lummi collects AI-generated pictures in a searchable library, organized by category and style. Users browse or search for backgrounds, textures, scenes, and illustrations, then download them for use in websites, presentations, and campaigns. The pitch is variety and a modern look compared with familiar stock photography.

The platform includes generation tools that let users create images from prompts and adjust them, along with options for editing. It is popular with designers who want unusual or abstract visuals and do not want to prompt from scratch.

item.title: Mutiny
item.description:
Mutiny changes what a website says depending on the visitor. If a visitor comes from a target account, an industry, or a campaign, Mutiny swaps in headlines, proof points, and calls to action that fit, using firmographic data and ad information. Marketers set this up in a visual editor without developers.

AI recommends segments and generates alternative copy, then tests variations and reports on conversions. Integrations connect with CRMs, ad platforms, and customer data tools so personalization can follow account-based marketing programs.

item.title: Nanonets
item.description:
Nanonets turns documents into data. A company sends invoices, purchase orders, receipts, or forms by email or upload, and the platform reads them, extracts fields and line items, and validates them against rules. Approved data flows into accounting or ERP systems.

Pre-trained models cover common documents, and teams can train models for their own layouts with a few samples. Workflows add approval steps, matching against purchase orders, and exception handling. Language models help with messy or varied documents.

item.title: Octane AI
item.description:
Octane AI lets stores add an interactive quiz to their site. Shoppers answer questions about preferences, and the quiz recommends products and captures their answers and contact details. Because customers volunteer the information, it is called zero-party data, and it supports personalized email and text marketing.

The platform integrates with Shopify and marketing tools such as Klaviyo, so quiz results can feed segments and flows. Brands use it for skincare, supplements, food, and other categories where choosing among many products is hard. Analytics show how quizzes affect conversion.

item.title: Patronus AI
item.description:
Patronus AI helps teams find problems in AI applications. Developers run test sets through their systems, and Patronus scores the outputs with evaluators that check for hallucinations, unsafe content, leaks of sensitive data, and policy violations. Red-teaming tools probe for weaknesses with adversarial inputs.

The company has published benchmarks, including tests for financial question answering, and trained evaluation models such as a judge model for hallucination detection. Monitoring features watch production traffic and alert teams to drops in quality.

item.title: PearAI
item.description:
PearAI is a standalone editor forked from VS Code, with AI features built in. Developers get code completion, a chat panel that understands the project, and inline editing, and can connect their preferred models. Because it is a fork, familiar extensions and settings carry over.

It positions itself as an open alternative to Cursor and Windsurf. The AI layer builds on Continue, an open-source assistant. The project had a licensing controversy early on regarding its use of existing code, which it has since addressed.

item.title: Phenom
item.description:
Phenom helps employers attract and manage talent. Its career sites show candidates jobs and content tailored to their interests, a recruiting CRM nurtures talent pools, and tools handle scheduling, chat, and applications. The same platform supports employees through internal job matching and career paths.

AI infers skills from resumes and profiles to match people with roles, recommend jobs, and surface candidates already in the system. Analytics show the hiring funnel and diversity data. The company sells to large enterprises.

item.title: Pory
item.description:
Pory turns spreadsheets and databases into websites. A user connects an Airtable base or Google Sheet, designs pages and layouts with a visual editor, and publishes a directory, portal, or dashboard. Logins and permissions control who sees what.

It is popular for member directories, job boards, simple CRMs, and client portals. Because the data stays in the source, updating the spreadsheet updates the site.

Pory has a free tier and paid plans. Complex logic is limited compared with full app builders. Alternatives include Softr, Glide, Stacker, Noloco, and Bubble. Pory suits non-developers building front ends on Airtable or Sheets.

item.title: Preply
item.description:
Preply matches students with tutors. Learners browse profiles, filter by language, price, and availability, book a trial lesson, and then continue with a tutor of their choice. Lessons take place on the platform’s video classroom with tools for sharing materials.

The company has added AI to support learning between lessons. Speaking practice partners simulate conversation, summaries and homework are generated from lessons, and vocabulary tools help with review. Tutors can use AI to prepare materials.

item.title: Sapling
item.description:
Sapling helps support and sales teams write faster and more consistently. As an agent types in the help desk or CRM, Sapling suggests completions based on past replies, fixes grammar and tone, and inserts approved snippets. This reduces typing time and variation.

Managers use quality analytics to monitor response times and consistency, and see how suggestions are used. It integrates with Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom, and other tools, and offers an API and an AI content detector.

item.title: Sloyd
item.description:
Sloyd takes a different approach from mesh generators. Its models are parametric, so a user can generate a chair or a sword and then adjust sliders for size, shape, and style, and get clean, game-ready geometry with proper topology. Real-time generation fits into workflows and game engines.
